Inventory.description: Read-only host observations; byte quantities are bytes, CPU count is logical CPUs, timestamps are RFC3339 UTC. NIC state describes a local link, not end-to-end reachability. VM state is observed libvirt state, not guest application health. Null lists mean no observations supplied. Controller retains newer inventory resource timestamps and independently newer per-check timestamps; a newer report sequence does not freshen an unchanged or older sample.

connection.description: unknown before any report, fresh within configured stale threshold, stale otherwise, revoked after administrator revocation. Restart cannot establish freshness from persisted wall-clock time alone. Controller default stale threshold is 30 seconds and is configurable; this is not a failure or failover deadline.

last_seen.description: Controller wall-clock receipt time of newest accepted report; null until a report arrives. Freshness is tracked using elapsed time in the active process.

capabilities.description: Last accepted sequenced report capabilities; managed-vm-v1 is required for new managed-VM work. Host connectivity freshness is checked separately.

csr_pem.description: Signed PEM CERTIFICATE REQUEST using an ECDSA P-256 key; no trailing PEM data.

hostname.description: Nonblank, maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes, no CR/LF/NUL.

host_id.description: Host-owned identity: the UUID this host generated on its first enrollment (canonical lowercase form) and keeps across Controllers. Hosts enrolled before host-owned identity present their Controller-issued 64-hex ID instead. Omitted only by older agents; the Controller then mints one.

pool_id.description: UUID of the pool this host is master of, generated by the host with host_id and kept across Controllers. Omitted by older agents or hosts that adopted a Controller-minted pool before presenting one; the Controller then mints or keeps the pool.

pool_name.description: Name of the pool held by the pool master, its hostname at first enrollment. Nonblank, maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes, no CR/LF/NUL. Defaults to hostname when omitted.

host_id.description: Equals the presented host_id when one was presented.

pool_id.description: Pool the host is master of; equals the presented pool_id when one was presented. Absent from rotation responses.

pool_name.description: Name of that pool. Absent from rotation responses.

csr_pem.description: Signed PEM CERTIFICATE REQUEST using an ECDSA P-256 key; no trailing PEM data.

vm.description: The full VM definition for vm-create (revision 0) and vm-update (revision current + 1).

image_update.description: Set on a host-image-update command: the action for this host's own update engine.

system_disk_replace.description: Set on a host-system-disk-replace command: the replacement disk for this host's system disk.

replace_repository.description: backup-repository-register: the repository ID typed to confirm replacing the credential or SFTP host key of an existing registration.

Command.description: Snapshot-create commands carry bounded snapshot name and description metadata; OperationID is the stable snapshot ID.

error.description: At most 4096 UTF-8 bytes; omit for successful checks.

observed_at.description: Agent-reported result time; controller operation updated_at records receipt/commit time. Not proof of guest application health.

version.description: The single report protocol version; any other value is refused with 409. A Core starts storage negotiation without storage-repositories-v1, waits for storage_repositories acknowledgement, persists it, then advertises the capability.

inventory.description: Omit or null for heartbeat only; prior inventory remains unchanged and is not made healthy.

capabilities.description: Advertised on every report. managed-vm-v1 enables managed command delivery. storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1 offers the additive clustered session-monitor projection; it must be acknowledged through storage_clusters_support before Core sends that projection. Omission or null disables managed delivery for this report; a newer sequence also replaces stored capabilities. vm-cpu-baseline-v1 advertises generic fixed CPU feature support and native pool baseline discovery; upgrade Controller before Core for additive fields.

storage_discoveries.description: One-shot sanitized results from prior report-response discovery requests. Never journaled or adopted.

storage_clusters.description: Transient results for addressed clustered-storage requests, emitted only after the exact v2 storage_clusters_support acknowledgement. session_monitor_ready and monitor-stage members are included only after the offered storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1 extension is acknowledged. The result exposes Core-owned durable operation state but is not Controller state.

pool_results.description: Answers to the pool_requests this host received on an earlier report response. More than 32 results is a malformed report (400). The Controller matches each result to its one pending in-memory request and keeps nothing afterwards.

ReportRequest.description: Version and sequence are required by runtime validation. Results may be omitted or null and defaults to no results. Inventory may be omitted or null for heartbeat only. Clustered results and storage-clustered-iscsi-v2 are withheld until this Controller connection acknowledges storage_clusters_support. The additive session-monitor members are withheld unless the Core offered and the Controller acknowledged storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1. Both acknowledgements reset after a cluster preflight failure, reconnect or Controller re-enrolment. Version-one reports retain existing non-storage behavior.

consoles.description: Console pairings to attach now; omitted when none. Not durable operations: they are delivered once and never journaled.

credential_offers.description: Opaque, addressed offers only; no credential bytes.

storage_repositories.description: Controller-first acknowledgement of protocol v2 storage support.

storage_clusters_support.description: Controller acknowledgement for the clustered v2 envelope. The base capability enables clustered results; storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1 is returned only when the Core offered it and enables the additive session-monitor report projection.

storage_discoveries.description: One-shot addressed Core observations. Controller removes each request from its bounded relay on delivery.

storage_clusters.description: One-shot addressed relay requests for a Core that has acknowledged and advertises storage-clustered-iscsi-v2. Controller deletes them after delivery, completion, cancellation, or deadline.

stats_channels.description: One-shot enrolled host reverse-channel request for usage history, hardware or backup inventory pages; delivered when the host offered the matching capability and a client query needs the channel.

pool_requests.description: One-shot addressed pool requests for a Core reporting protocol v2. Delivered once and never journaled; the Controller takes each pending request out of its bounded in-memory broker as it sends it, so a lost response simply expires and the operator retries.

iso_download_progress.description: True only in a v2 response to a Core offering iso-download-progress-v1. Core withholds ManagedState.iso_downloads until acknowledged, and clears readiness on disconnect, restart or Controller replacement.

detected_os.description: True only in a v2 response to a Core offering detected-os-v1. Core withholds ManagedState.detected_os until acknowledged; startup and re-enrollment clear readiness without erasing retained history.

image_update.description: True only in a v2 response to a Core offering image-update-v1 (offered only by a host whose update engine is running). Core withholds Inventory.image and the host-image-update commands until acknowledged and clears readiness on disconnect, restart or Controller replacement, so a strict older Controller never sees the field.

resource_id.description: The resource the action applied to, such as a site, pool, host or VM ID. VM requests record the VM ID; older vm-power, vm-media, vm-update and vm-delete rows keep an operation or internal row ID.

detail.description: Actionable detail for debounced health transitions when present.

password.description: Existing administrator password, at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes. Existing password hashes remain valid.

name.description: Nonblank after trimming whitespace; at most 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR, LF, or NUL.

host_id.description: Optional revoked host to re-enroll; its pool must belong to site_id.

address.description: Hostname or IP, optionally with :port (default 9443). No scheme, path, or userinfo.

fingerprint.description: sha256:<64 lowercase hex characters> over the leaf certificate's DER encoding.

subject.description: Leaf certificate subject, for operator confirmation only.

address.description: Hostname or IP, optionally with :port (default 9443). No scheme, path, or userinfo.

fingerprint.description: sha256:<64 lowercase hex characters>, as returned by probeHost and confirmed by the operator.

root_password.description: Used once to sign in to the host's local API; never stored, logged, or echoed. 1-1024 bytes, no NUL.

controller_url.description: This Controller's own HTTPS origin, reachable from the host, given to it as its enrollment target.

host_id.description: Optional revoked host to re-enroll; its pool must belong to this site.

pool_id.description: The automatic pool the enrollment created or, on re-enrollment, kept.

host_id.description: Present when the host reported it is already enrolled.

request_id.description: Nonblank after trimming whitespace; at most 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR, LF, or NUL.

enrollment_token.description: Caller-generated secret persisted before sending; never log or expose in operation results.

pool_id.description: Optional; when supplied it must equal the host's pool.

vm_id.description: Stable lowercase nonzero libvirt UUID; adoption preserves identity.

guest.description: Latest host guest observation for a VM observed running in a fresh report; omitted otherwise.

usage.description: Host observation of a running VM's resource consumption; absent for VMs that are not running, from Core builds that predate usage observation, and whenever the host could not sample the VM within its probe deadline.

detected_os.description: Historical OS identity from the pool master; may remain available when the VM is stopped or its live guest observation is absent. Display as last detected when no live OS is reported. Older Core builds omit it.

ManagedAppliance.description: Unified VM listing. Existing adopted appliances preserve role=controller and protected=true without creation spec/status. Generic guest entries add spec and operation_id/status/error; state/freshness always come from fresh successful libvirt observations independently of creation status.

directory.description: Validated existing relative subdirectory beneath the original NFS export; spaces are supported, traversal, backslashes and control characters are rejected.

mount_path.description: Original existing ZFS dataset mount path. It rejects Unicode whitespace/control characters, percent and backslash because Core uses it as a systemd What value.

share.description: Ordinary share name: letters, numbers, internal spaces and ._$:()-; no leading/trailing whitespace or path/command/unit syntax.

directory.description: Validated existing relative subdirectory below the SMB share, including spaces; never an SMB path. Traversal, backslashes and control characters are rejected.

ISCSIStorageSource.description: exclusive is the legacy single-writer profile and needs exclusive_target. clustered_gfs2 instead requires cluster_id, lock_table and three to five unique eligible hosts, rejects exclusive_target, and only accepts an existing GFS2 filesystem; Core never formats it.

ISCSIStorageSourceIntent.description: Client iSCSI intent. Core chooses mount_path only after allocating the repository ID.

StorageSourceIntent.description: Non-secret client source selection. Exactly one backend is required for a typed repository.

filesystem_id.description: New Core-observed identities use the NFSv4 kernel protocol FSID profile nfs4:<mounted-server-address-hex>:<port-hex>:<fsid-major-hex>:<fsid-minor-hex>. Core binds that profile to stat.Dev and one matching /proc/fs/nfsfs/volumes row, then verifies the requested source. Missing or ambiguous rows fail closed; a zero protocol FSID is valid. Address changes fail closed and are not NFS HA failover. Preserved legacy statfs identities remain representable, are not auto-upgraded, and fail closed.
Diagnostic CIFS filesystem ID; it is not durable across reconnects.

marker_id.description: Core-created atomic durable share-root marker for new registrations. Core verifies it with the exact SMB source/options after reconnect. Absent only on preserved legacy records, which retain strict filesystem-ID failure behavior and are not auto-upgraded.

username.description: Management-controller account for redfish and ipmilan, with power control only. It is not a secret and is reported back; its password is the credential. Absent on virsh and scsi_pr profiles, and a BMC profile without one can never produce a proof.

tls_fingerprint.description: Core captures the certificate the controller presents when the profile is recorded, keeps its leaf SHA-256 here and holds every later connection to exactly it: a factory management controller is self-signed with no usable name, so this pin, not a chain, identifies the endpoint the password is sent to and the power-off is issued through. A changed certificate refuses the fence with its own sentence rather than as a network fault. Reported so an operator can compare it with the controller's own page; it is not a secret and a client never supplies one. Absent on ipmilan, which authenticates its RMCP+ session and presents no certificate, and on virsh and scsi_pr.

virsh_uri.description: For virsh, exactly qemu:///system or qemu+ssh://<ssh_login>@<endpoint>[:<ssh_port>]/system. The latter must match the pinned SSH fields; it rejects passwords, query strings, fragments and every other URI path. An omitted URI port is valid only when ssh_port is 22.

cipher.description: The RMCP+ cipher suite an ipmilan fence must use, as the controller's own LAN channel offers it. Core selects it itself — 17 where the controller offers it, otherwise 3, the suite every IPMI 2.0 controller must implement — either while provisioning the account in-band or while proving a profile an operator entered. Suite 0 asks for no authentication, no integrity and no confidentiality, so it is never selected and never accepted here. Absent means none was recorded and ipmitool's own default is used. A client never supplies it; a request that does is refused with 400.

provisioned_by_core.description: The account behind this profile is one Nex Core created on the host's own management controller in-band. It is how a host knows, after a reboot or a master change, that the account under the Nex name is its own to replace rather than somebody else's to leave alone, and it is why an operator-entered profile is never overwritten by automatic provisioning. Written only by the pool master when the host's own Core reports the account it created; a client never supplies it, and a request that does is refused with 400.

StorageClusterFence.description: Closed Core fence profile. credential_ref and ssh_host_key_ref are opaque names for root-only Core secrets, never secret bytes; arbitrary commands and arguments are not accepted. Before any power-off Core asks the management controller which machine it manages — the Redfish ComputerSystem.UUID, compared exactly, or IPMI Get System GUID, where either documented byte order counts — and compares it with the target host's own SMBIOS system UUID in the master's membership record. A mismatch, a host with no unique hardware identity and an unreadable controller each refuse the fence and power nothing off. Redirects are never followed, so the identity cannot be read from one machine while another is powered off. A Redfish fence is performed by Core itself over the pinned connection — identity GET, ComputerSystem.Reset ForceOff, then a separate PowerState read — rather than by fence_redfish, which cannot be bound to the recorded certificate. virsh is for a Nex Core running as a virtual machine in a disposable lab and remains unaccepted for native production use.

request_id.description: Optional stable ID of the actual destructive fence attempt. A Core verifies this binding before accepting a peer receipt.

method.description: How the exclusion was proved. Absent is a fence device Nex Core powered the host off through and independently observed off, which is every proof there was before watchdog fencing. watchdog is the host resetting itself, whose evidence is the record beside it. A clustered-storage fence only ever produces the absent one.

watchdog.description: The evidence of a watchdog exclusion, present only when method says so.

storage_lease.description: Native exclusion evidence shape; not currently enabled as an accepted promotion proof path.

StorageClusterFenceStatus.description: Core-recorded result of an actual fence/exclusion observation, bound to a request ID when destructive work was attempted and to an exact configuration generation and digest.

StorageClusterConfig.description: Core-owned clustered-GFS2 projection. Controller relay input never grants a caller-owned device path, mount path, proof, or secret; Core derives/verifies those native details.

session_monitor_ready.description: Authenticated member attestation that the fixed local transport-monitor wrapper and CLI are installed and passed a successful live exact portal/IQN session probe. It is distinct from aggregate GFS2 or cluster health, and is projected to Controller only after storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1 is acknowledged.

StorageClusterRequest.description: Authenticated Controller/Core report envelope. It is transient at Controller; Core persists accepted configuration and operation state.

StorageClusterCredentialRef.description: Secret-free reference to a one-time Core credential handoff.

StorageClusterOperation.description: v2 operation projection. members are typed host-bound reports, never an unordered flattened status list. degraded is a Core-observed post-activation runtime state, not an activation receipt or client action.

StorageClusterMemberReport.description: Core-observed member report bound to one configured host and exact clustered-storage configuration. monitor is sent only after the offered storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1 extension is acknowledged. The Controller rejects duplicate, non-member or mismatched bindings.

expected_generation.description: Optional optimistic generation. Omit or use zero for a candidate repository whose Core allocation has not yet assigned a generation.

StorageClusterCredentialRequest.description: One-time secret handoff. secret is bounded to 64 KiB and is never returned; username is optional.

shared.description: Core-observed shared-storage capability, never by itself permission to place or start a VM. Provisioned ZFS is always false because each selected host has an independent local zpool.

ResourceLifecycleRequest.description: network-remove, network-update and media-remove payload. Registration keeps the Command.network/Command.media shape, whose resource ID is reserved permanently on the host; a lifecycle change takes its own operation slot (network-lifecycle:<resource_id>:<operation_id>, media-lifecycle:<resource_id>:<operation_id>), so a removal never collides with the registration that created the resource. kind is always resource + "-" + action, so media-update does not exist. Core validates the same shape Controller does.

action.description: update is a rename and applies to a network only.

host_id.description: The host Core applies this to: always the pool master for a pool VLAN, and the reported owner for an imported ISO. Controller resolves it; clients do not send it.

expected_generation.description: Required and at least 1. Core refuses a request whose generation is no longer current; 0 on the wire is read as 1 for records written before generations existed.

name.description: New network name; update only, nonblank, at most 200 UTF-8 bytes, no slashes or control characters. A removal must not carry one.

StorageCredentials.description: Transient credential bytes only. Optional domain is the SMB workgroup or AD domain used with username/secret. The selected operation validates the applicable secret form; inventory, journals, results and diagnostics never carry these fields.

target_iqn.description: Optional for kind iscsi only. Omit to discover targets; supply a previously selected IQN to inspect its LUNs. Requires storage-iscsi-inspect-v1 on the addressed Core. Inspection CHAP secrets are limited to 255 UTF-8 bytes and rejected before relay when too long.

purpose.description: Optional. backup makes an SMB candidate's existing flag report a backup repository's owner marker instead of VM storage's marker. Valid only for kinds nfs and smb (400 otherwise); requires storage-discovery-purpose-v1 on the addressed Core (409 otherwise, because an older Core silently ignores the field).

spares.description: Hot spares. They are erased like the data disks, added as spare vdevs and the pool is created with autoreplace=on, so ZFS resilvers onto one by itself when a data disk fails. They satisfy no part of the layout rule.

ZFSProvisionAPIRequest.description: Core allocates repository_id when omitted. Supplying a Core-owned repository_id configures selected hosts for that existing pool-scoped repository.

ZFSProvisionHostResult.description: Durable outcome for one selected host. pool_guid and dataset_guid identify that host's independent native zpool and dataset after a successful provision; this outcome alone is not a current access observation.

ZFSReplaceRequest.description: Replace one failed leaf device of a provisioned ZFS repository's pool on one host. old_device names the leaf exactly as the pool observation reports it, and device is one candidate from POST /api/v1/storage/discover with kind zfs-device, carrying the same identity, fingerprint and typed erase confirmation rules the ZFS wizard uses. Core revalidates both against a fresh observation of the pool and the disk before it touches anything.

operation_id.description: Core operation identity. The executing host journals its replacement under it, so a redelivered command replays the recorded outcome instead of acting again.

host_id.description: The configured host whose pool holds the failed disk. It may be the pool master or a ready current member.

old_device.description: The failed leaf's /dev/disk/by-id path, as the repository's pool observation reports it.

ZFSReplaceAPIRequest.description: The Controller allocates the operation ID; request_id is the client's own stable retry key.

ZFSHostAccess.description: Current per-host observation for a Core-provisioned local ZFS repository. The GUIDs, path, capacity and read/write flags apply only to host_id; a missing or errored observation grants no placement permission.

ZFSPoolStatus.description: Core's transient `zpool status` observation of one imported pool. Nothing durable is derived from it: the Controller passes it through and a fresh Controller sees it again on the next report.

ZFSPoolScan.description: A running or completed scrub or resilver. ZFS formats its own sizes and timestamps, so they are reported as the strings it produced.

parent.description: replacing or spare when this leaf sits under an in-flight replacement or activated-spare vdev; omitted for an ordinary data leaf.

ZFSPoolDevice.description: One leaf of the pool's vdev tree, named as the pool was created: the /dev/disk/by-id path for a Core-provisioned repository. parent marks an in-flight replacing or spare vdev.

iscsi_luns.description: Selected-target iSCSI observations. Absent on a succeeded inspection means no block LUNs were reported (empty results are omitted); absent on older Core and on target-only discovery. At most 64 entries with unique lun values, and only on a succeeded result; a target reporting more than 64 LUNs is refused instead of capped. Missing identities are unknown, not defaults.

ISCSILUNDiscovery.description: One read-only Core observation of a selected target's LUN. Zero is valid. LUN numbers retain native Linux HCTL addressing, including flat-addressing bits, so the observed identity can be registered without selecting another LUN. Filesystem identity is supplied only when native probing identifies one unambiguous filesystem; error explains partial or unsupported observations.

retire_eligible.description: Core's current redacted eligibility observation. Core rechecks references before a retire command takes effect.

StorageClusterSupport.description: Controller-first acknowledgement for the clustered-storage v2 envelope. Return storage-cluster-session-monitor-v1 only when the Core offered it; otherwise return storage-clustered-iscsi-v2.

hostname.description: Host-reported name retained in the Core master membership and signed replica so a fresh Controller can name an offline member. At most 200 UTF-8 bytes of printable characters.

observed_at.description: When the master admitted this member, or created the pool for its founding host. Nothing rewrites it afterwards; the Controller reports it as joined_at.

peer_origin.description: Bare HTTPS origin this member advertised to the master for peer traffic. Recorded from the member's own advertisement, or, for the master's own row, from the master_url of the first Controller-driven join, which the master works out itself when none is supplied; never inferred from Controller connectivity.

system_uuid.description: This host's own SMBIOS system UUID, 32 lower-case hex digits without separators, reported by the host itself while it was alive: at join, and on every reconcile pass, so a pool formed before this existed gains it without re-joining. It is what proves a management controller belongs to this machine before it is powered off. Like peer_origin it is a recorded observation and moves no generation. A host too old to report one stays empty and simply cannot be given a BMC fence device.

replica_ack_excluded.description: Core-owned exclusion from snapshot reservation/settlement replica acknowledgements and ordinary replica-push failure aggregation, recorded only by a supported promotion after validating fresh exact fence evidence. Omitted means false. The host remains a pool member and VM owner; delivery is still attempted. The master clears the exclusion only after accepted current-membership VM inventory and an exact current-generation/content replica POST acknowledgement. Covered by the signed authority content, without changing membership generation when cleared. It does not exempt destructive resource-removal acknowledgements, storage-lease preparation, restart authority confirmation or future promotion fencing. Use matching development Core builds; old promotions are not retroactively excluded.

replica_generation.description: The master's observation of the authority-replica generation this member last acknowledged. Memory-only on the master and overlaid on the reported copy of the membership record: it is never written into the durable membership and is never an input to the generation equality rule. A member that has never acknowledged one is reported at 0, honestly.

replica_digest.description: Content digest the member acknowledged, as observed by the master.

replica_error.description: The master's bounded reason for the last failed push to this member: "pool member did not report its authority replica", "pool member did not acknowledge the authority replica", "pool member acknowledged the replica without joining the authority sanlock lockspace", "pool member acknowledged the replica without the Corosync key", "pool member refused the authority replica" or the member's own refusal text, "pool authority replica exceeds the peer body limit", or "pool member peer certificate cannot receive a wrapped pool CA key", "pool member did not report backup authority page progress", "pool member reported invalid backup authority page progress", "pool member refused backup authority page reuse", "pool member refused a backup authority page", or a refusal to report/stage a signed backup authority page.

replica_observed_at.description: When the master made that observation. Zero when it has none.

fence.description: How this host would be excluded from the pool if it had to be fenced: the same closed typed profile clustered storage already uses, recorded in the master's durable membership and replicated with it, so a promoted master inherits it and a fresh Controller re-adopts it. Only a virsh profile can be recorded by this build; Core refuses to record a profile it cannot verify. The credential reference it carries is never projected to a client, and neither is anything the reference names.

fence_credential_version.description: The master's counter for the private fence credential material behind this host's profile. The material itself is never in the membership; only this number is, so rotating it changes the replicated content and therefore advances the pool authority generation, while re-recording identical material moves nothing.

fence_readiness.description: The pool master's own answer to whether this host could be shut out, per method. Reported only by the master, only for the membership it owns, and never written into the durable record. Absent from a Core too old to report it, which a Controller shows as "not reported" and never as ready.

system_uuid_conflict_host_id.description: The member that already reported the hardware identity this host reports, when the master refused this host's report because of it. Without it the refusal is a dead end: an operator is told their host has no unique identity with nothing to act on. Cleared the moment the identity is accepted.

bmc.description: What this host's own Core found and did about its own management controller, reported to the master over the existing advertise peer route. It is an observation and a result, never a credential.

bmc_provisioning_disabled.description: The operator's own decision, recorded by the master, that this host must not configure its management controller for fencing. Clearing a fence device Nex Core provisioned sets it — one operator action with one meaning — and the host removes the account it created when it sees it. It is a decision, not an observation, so it lives with the fence profile in the replicated membership and a host cannot set or clear it by reporting about itself.

watchdog.description: This host's own watchdog capability, reported by the host and recorded by the master. A member too old to report one leaves it null, which is never counted.

watchdog_armed.description: That host's own report that it has armed its watchdog, recorded durably by the master. Null means the host never said, which is never a watchdog exclusion proof.

sanlock_host_id.description: Pool-master-assigned stable sanlock host ID. Zero or absent means this legacy member cannot participate in a storage lease.

sanlock_host_generation.description: Last native sanlock generation this host itself observed while its configured lease ID was live; not a proof by itself.

host_fencing_disabled.description: The pool's Host fencing setting, recorded the way it is decided: fencing is on for a pool that has never been told otherwise, so an absent field is on and a record written before the setting existed keeps the default. It is a decision, so it is durable, replicated and only ever written by the master.

fence_summary.description: The pool's fencing count, setting and prerequisite checklist, computed by the master over this membership when it reports it. Like the readiness on each member row it is a memory-only observation overlaid on the reported copy and never part of the durable record.

witness.description: The master's durable qdevice witness selection and CA pin. Runtime readiness is re-established from the native cluster after restart.

next_sanlock_host_id.description: Monotonic host-ID allocator watermark; prevents reuse after a member is ejected.

storage_lease.description: Reserved durable storage-lease configuration. The current product does not expose an accepted operator setup or automatic promotion workflow for it.

membership.description: The full membership record for the pool actions that carry one. For join and maintenance only master_host_id is set: the master reads its own record, and a membership composed in the Controller could already be stale.

expected_version.description: The membership generation the operator saw. 0 or absent means unchecked. For action maintenance it is compared against the master's own current membership generation, not against the membership on the wire.

member_host_id.description: For action join, the joining host: it is the command's target, and the pool-join command is the one pool command not delivered to the master. For action maintenance it names the host being drained, which is not the target: that command goes to the master, addressed by membership.master_host_id.

enabled.description: For action maintenance, the desired drain state of member_host_id. It is a desired state, not a transition: re-sending the state the host is already in succeeds and leaves maintenance_since unmoved.

master_url.description: Bare HTTPS origin of the master's pool-peer listener that the joining Core dials. Required for action join.

pool_ca_pem.description: Master's pool CA, pinned by the joining Core for the peer exchange. Required for action join. Never returned by any Controller read route.

invitation.description: Single-use, 15-minute, pool- and host-bound join credential issued by the master and redeemed by the joining Core itself. Required for action join. The Controller relays it and never returns, lists, logs or audits it; the stored command row is scrubbed of this field and pool_ca_pem as soon as the operation leaves queued, and unconditionally 15 minutes after issue.

peer_origin.description: Optional bare HTTPS origin the joining host advertises to its new master after it is admitted.

fence.description: The power-fence profile to record for member_host_id, on action fence-profile. null clears the recorded profile. Any credential the operator supplied has already been delivered to Core over the one-time encrypted credential handoff before this command is written, and only the opaque reference Core allocated appears here.

fence_confirmed.description: The operator's separate, explicit acknowledgement that promoting this candidate powers the old pool master off. It is a precondition and nothing else: Core produces and verifies the fence proof itself, no proof ever crosses this wire, and an acknowledgement is never evidence of anything.

fence_host_ids.description: The exact set of hosts the operator agreed to power off, as the verdict's fence_host_ids named them. Core compares it against the set it computes again at run time and refuses the promotion if they differ, so the fence can never widen between the confirmation and the act.

update.description: Request of the update-rollout and update-control actions.

PoolCommand.description: membership is required for the member-join and storage-reconcile actions and is absent for join and maintenance: a joining host is not a member yet, and the master reads its own membership rather than trusting a Controller mirror. Valid() requires request_id plus, for action join, member_host_id, master_url, pool_ca_pem and invitation within the lengths above.

request_id.description: Stable client-generated idempotency key. Reuse it verbatim to retry; any changed field conflicts.

host_id.description: The enrolled host to add. It must currently be the master of its own single-host pool.

peer_origin.description: Bare https origin (scheme, host and port only, no path, query, fragment or userinfo) the joining host will advertise to its new master, for example https://192.0.2.12:9444. At most one trailing "/" is accepted and normalised away, exactly as the host-local join route accepts it; the normalised slash-less form is stored and forwarded, so the two spellings are the same request for exact-retry replay rather than a changed payload.

master_url.description: Optional bare https origin of the master's pool-peer listener. Ignored when the master has already advertised its own peer origin. When omitted the master works out its own origin from its configured pool-peer listener (the listener's port, and its address when bound to one; the default-route source address for a wildcard bind), and refuses the join if it has no default route; masters built before this rule refuse an omitted master_url. At most one trailing "/" is accepted and normalised away, exactly as the host-local join route accepts it; the normalised slash-less form is stored and forwarded, so the two spellings are the same request for exact-retry replay rather than a changed payload.

host_id.description: The joining host the command was addressed to.

PoolJoinAccepted.description: Deliberately narrow: who was asked to join and the durable operation that asked. It never carries the invitation, the pool CA or the master URL.

master_seen_at.description: When the pool master host last reported to this Controller, RFC3339, or "" when it has never reported. It is this Controller's own record of a host report, never a pool fact, projected from the hosts row it already keeps, so nothing new is stored for it. It is deliberately not gated on freshness: a stale-master banner needs exactly "has not reported since <master_seen_at>", and a fresh Controller that has never heard from the master says so rather than inventing a time.

generation.description: Membership generation as reported by the master; 0 when the master has reported no membership.

authoritative.description: True only while master_connection is fresh. When false, every observational master-reported field — status, error, checks, access counts, failures, maintenance and maintenance_since — is blank, null or unknown and must be presented as unknown rather than as the last known good state. peer_origin, the member's own reported join, its guests and the Controller's own last_maintenance are not master observations and are still reported.

authority.description: The pool master's own reported authority record, mirrored verbatim. null when the master is not fresh or reports none. It is the only absolute generation in the pool; the Controller derives none.

transfer.description: The pool master's own report of a transfer. null when the master is not fresh or reports none: a stale master's last transfer is never shown as present truth. Each participant's own view is on its member row.

last_transfer.description: The newest pool-transfer command this Controller relayed for this pool, so an asynchronous Core refusal is visible where the operator acted. null when there is none.

master_conflict.description: Host IDs whose reported membership contradicts the recorded master without being evidence this Controller may adopt, which is exactly two cases: a host whose own membership names itself master at exactly the generation mirrored for the recorded master, and a host reporting a strictly higher generation for a master that is neither itself nor the recorded one. A strictly higher generation reported by the very host its membership names as master is the adoption rule's evidence and is followed rather than shown, and a fenced old master reporting at its old, strictly lower generation is not a rival claim at all. Normally empty; never acted on, only shown.

promotion.description: A candidate's own reported fence-verified promotion, mirrored verbatim and stored nowhere. null when no fresh host of this pool reports one.

last_promotion.description: The newest pool-promote command this Controller relayed for the pool, so an asynchronous Core refusal is visible where the operator acted. conflict marks refusals a synchronous route would have answered with 409; retryable is always false for a promotion, because nothing about one is retried unchanged — the blocking condition has to change first.

fence.description: The pool's own fencing answer as the master reported it with its membership. Mirrored verbatim and stored nowhere; null when the master is not fresh or is too old to report one, which reads as not reported and never as ready.

name.description: Host name from the enrolled host when known, otherwise from Core-owned membership; falls back to the stable host ID for a legacy record without a name. An offline member need not have an enrolled Controller host row.

status.description: The master's own membership status for this host. unknown when the master is not fresh, and for the synthesised single row shown when the master has reported no membership at all.

peer_origin.description: Part of the master's durable membership record, not an observation of it: it is how this member is reached, and a quiet master does not make it untrue, so it is reported whether or not authoritative is true. Empty when the master has recorded none.

joined_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC time the pool master admitted this member, or created the pool for its founding host: the observed_at of the master's durable membership record, which nothing rewrites after admission. Like peer_origin it is a record, reported whether or not authoritative is true. Empty when the reported record has none. Introduced in development product 0.4.8.

checks.description: The four convergence checks this host itself reported: pool-storage-reconciliation, pool-network-reconciliation, pool-media-reconciliation and pool-authority-replica. Empty while authoritative is false.

failures.description: Per-member resource failures: the master's failed member_access rows, plus uplink rows derived from this member's own reported NICs against each pool VLAN, deduplicated against the master's failure for the same network.

join.description: This member's own reported inventory.managed.join, or null when it reports none.

replica.description: null on the pool master's own row.

maintenance.description: The master's durable drain flag for this host. null whenever authoritative is false: unknown, never assumed false.

maintenance_since.description: RFC3339 UTC since when this host has been drained; empty when it is not drained, or while authoritative is false.

last_maintenance.description: The newest pool-maintenance operation this Controller holds for this member, or null. It is Controller-held operation history, not master-reported state, so it is present whether or not the master is fresh.

transfer.description: This host's own report of the master change or eject it is part of, with role source, target or ejected. null whenever the host is not reporting now: a participant whose row is null while connection is not fresh is unknown, not finished.

fence.description: What the master's membership records about how this host would be excluded. null while the master is not fresh, and null when no profile is recorded.

restricted.description: This host's own Core-enforced refusal to act on pool authority. It is the host's own report, so it is shown whenever that host is fresh, whatever the pool master is doing — a restricted old master is precisely a host reporting for itself in a pool whose master changed. null when the host is not fresh or reports no restriction.

name.description: A fixed list in a fixed order. A check the host does not report is projected as unknown, never omitted, so the column cannot silently lose a row; new checks are appended and existing positions do not move. The list is the host's own report, so it is present exactly while that host is fresh, whatever the pool master is doing.

pending.description: Pool resources for which this member has reported no access row yet.

stale.description: Access rows whose observation is older than the staleness bound.

PoolMemberAccessCounts.description: Counts of the master's member_access rows for this host across pool storage, networks and media. The master's own row carries no counts: member_access is the master's record about its members.

eligible.description: False if and only if some row is refuses_join. It is a preview of host-reported facts, not an authorization: Core decides again at submission.

peer_address.description: Host part of the peer origin this candidate reports for itself (inventory.managed.peer_origin), or empty when it reports none. The dialog shows and lets the operator edit only this.

peer_port.description: Port of that reported peer origin, or Core's default pool-peer port 9444 when the host reports none. The dialog composes peer_origin as https://<peer_address>:<peer_port>.

subject.description: What the row is about, for example the pool VLAN and its uplink NIC name.

endpoint.description: bmc-probe only: the management controller address, a bare host name or IP address.

username.description: bmc-probe only: the account to sign in with; present exactly when credential_ref is.

credential_ref.description: bmc-probe only: the opaque reference the one-time credential handoff returned for the password. The master retires the material once the probe has answered, whatever the outcome, and refuses a reference that names a recorded fence device.

PoolRequest.description: Transient Controller-to-master request carried in one report response, in the shape storage_clusters already uses. Sent only to a Core that reports protocol v2, and only when host_id is that reporting host. The master answers on its next report and the Controller keeps nothing afterwards.

PoolJoinInvitation.description: Master-issued, single-use, 15-minute credential the joining Core redeems against the master by itself. The master binds the presented CSR at first redemption, so the same invitation always returns the same member certificate and never admits a second member. It exists in Controller memory only for the remainder of the HTTP request that relays it and is never returned to a client, logged or audited.

promotion.description: The promotion candidate's verdict, answered to a promotion-preflight pool request. Nothing about it is stored by the Controller.

bmc_probe.description: The master's answer to a bmc-probe pool request. It may accompany a failed result, to say what did answer. Nothing about it is stored by the Controller.

PoolResult.description: The master's answer to one PoolRequest, on its next report. A result whose pool, host or request_id does not match the pending request, or which succeeded without an unexpired invitation, is discarded as if it had not arrived.

PoolJoinStatus.description: The joining host's own report of its durable staged join, persisted in its pool state directory and reported until it is ready, so a replaced Controller adopts an interrupted join instead of losing it. stage is the step still to perform; ready means every stage is done. A host that has been admitted but has not finished rehoming or advertising reports needs_attention, never success.

identity.description: Core-canonical secret-free identity observed after member preparation.

locking.description: Member proved the shared non-blocking lock against the master for this generation.

PoolStorageReservationRequest.description: Authenticated member-to-master peer request. The master binds the reservation to the mTLS member identity, not a client host field.

PoolStorageReservationRelease.description: Peer DELETE query shape. release_unused is used only by a member after its healthy serialized Core journal proves no managed VM disk or ISO reference remains.

zfs_host_access.description: Current local access observations for each configured host of a Core-provisioned ZFS repository.

zfs_provisioned.description: True only for a repository created through Core ZFS provisioning.

zfs_scope.description: Requested ZFS scope (host or pool). Pool scope shares the Core repository identity across independent host-local zpools; it does not make storage shared.

StorageRegistration.description: Core-owned repository configuration and observation. A repository has one selected host in this release; shared is a capability observation, never placement permission. Source identity, access, capacity and health are Core observations; a missing or replaced mount blocks writes and never falls back to a mountpoint. For existing-dataset ZFS registration, source.zfs.mount_path remains the existing dataset mount and path is the Core-owned /var/lib/nex-storage/<repository-id> bind alias used by VM disks; detach removes only that alias and never ZFS properties. Core ZFS provisioning creates its own tagged pool and vms dataset, then uses the same alias. Credentials remain Core-local and inventory reports only presence. A fresh Controller adopts these records from Inventory.managed.storage.

source.description: Bridge name used by guest interfaces (derived <uplink>v<vlan> for kind vlan) or libvirt network name.

uplink.description: Uplink NIC name: required for kind vlan; set on kind bridge when the registration was created automatically for the untagged network of a bridge on a physical port.

generation.description: kind vlan: master-owned desired generation members reconcile against; 0 on host-local registrations.

member_access.description: kind vlan: the master's observations of each member's applied bridge; absent on host-local registrations.

tombstone.description: The host durably removed this network. The row carries only id, pool_id, host_id and the generation after the removal; name, kind, source and the rest are absent. A Controller deletes its mirror row for that host and never re-adopts the registration from an older report, and a peer list never carries one.

NetworkRegistration.description: Pool guest network on one host: an existing bridge, an active libvirt network, or a Core-created VLAN bridge (kind vlan) on an uplink NIC. VLAN bridges are additive; the management bridge, addresses and routes are never changed. The host self-registers the untagged default network of every host bridge on a physical NIC or bond (<port> untagged, kind bridge, uplink recorded) in its own journal with host-generated IDs, at agent start and when a new uplink appears; Controller creates registrations itself only by adoption (actor system): any network the host reports in Inventory.managed.networks that Controller does not hold (request_id adopt-network:<host>:<id>, ID and name preserved). A bridge or libvirt network already held by another registration on that host is a failed host result, not an HTTP 409.

size_bytes.description: Zero until a URL download completes; applied media is at least 32774 bytes.

url.description: Command-only public HTTP(S) source URL. Omitted from client responses and applied host inventory. Requires iso-download-v1.

generation.description: Fences removal, as it does for storage and networks. Imports leave it zero and every reader treats zero as 1.

tombstone.description: The host durably removed this ISO and unlinked its published file. The row carries only id, pool_id, host_id and the generation after the removal; a Controller deletes its mirror row for that host and never re-adopts the import from an older report.

count.description: vCPUs presented to the guest. Both sides require at least 1; Controller caps the request at 64 and refuses more than the host reports.

sockets.description: Sockets, or 0 with cores and threads for the default topology.

cores.description: Cores per socket, or 0 for the default topology.

threads.description: Threads per core, or 0 for the default topology.

model.description: Host modes follow the current host; named models come from native host capabilities. New wizard drafts choose the current pool CPU baseline when available, storing its exact model/features. Explicit feature-bearing definitions are compared against the actual VM machine and runtime. Baseline compatibility covers current members only, not future hosts or live migration. CPU choices are independent of guest OS.

features.description: Optional fixed native CPU feature list. Omitted or empty retains model-only behavior. Nonempty requires a named model (not host modes or max) and vm-cpu-baseline-v1. Duplicate feature names are rejected.

VMCPU.description: vCPU count, optional topology and CPU model. Sockets, cores and threads all 0 select the default topology of one socket, count cores and one thread; otherwise each must be at least 1 and sockets × cores × threads must equal count. JSON Schema cannot express that product, so Controller and Core both enforce it in protocol.ValidateVMSpec.

mode.description: dedicated preallocates and locks the ceiling in host RAM while running: memory and currentMemory at size_mib, no balloon, and memoryBacking with immediate allocation, locked and nosharepages. Stopped VMs release physical RAM but retain their Nex capacity commitment. QEMU overhead is locked too. Requires updated Core; existing VMs need full shutdown, a successful stopped vm-update save and start. Legacy dedicated live edits fail before device effects with a stop-and-save instruction. Upgrade, autostart or guest reboot alone does not rewrite old definitions. maximum caps without reserving: the same ceiling plus a virtio balloon with free page reporting, so the guest returns pages it frees. Reclaim requires the balloon driver running in the guest (built into Linux; virtio-win guest tools on Windows); without it the guest drifts to the ceiling and holds it. There is no pressure-driven reclaim daemon.

size_mib.description: Memory ceiling in MiB. Both sides require at least 512; Controller caps the request at 262144.

VMMemory.description: Memory ceiling and how the host treats it. size_mib is the ceiling in both modes and host capacity preflight uses that ceiling in both modes: a VM that cannot reach its ceiling is refused. dedicated additionally counts against committed capacity; maximum reserves nothing and is allowed to oversubscribe.

storage_id.description: Registered storage that has succeeded on this VM's host and pool. Core resolves it by resource ID, not by pool/host ID, so it survives Controller replacement.

name.description: Operator-facing disk name, unique within the VM. Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore, starting with a letter or digit; it is not a path.

bus.description: virtio needs guest drivers (built into Linux, virtio-win on Windows); sata and scsi work without them.

thin.description: true creates a sparse qcow2 that grows on use; false preallocates the full size.

boot_order.description: 0 keeps the disk out of the boot order. Non-zero values are unique across every disk and boot.media_boot_order and number the boot devices from 1 with no gaps.

VMDisk.description: One virtual disk, created inside the VM's own exclusive directory on its storage target. Disks are never shared or reused: Core checks exclusive ownership for every disk and free space per storage target, summing the disks that land on the same target.

network_id.description: Registered network that has succeeded on this VM's host and pool, resolved by resource ID.

model.description: Which network card the guest sees. virtio is paravirtualised: fastest and lowest host CPU, but the guest needs a driver (built into Linux, virtio-win on Windows). e1000 and e1000e emulate Intel gigabit cards nearly every OS already drives, for guests and installers that cannot see a virtio adapter, at higher host CPU. rtl8139 emulates a 100 Mbit card for guests too old for a gigabit driver; the limit is the emulated hardware. vmxnet3 is VMware's paravirtualised adapter, for guests already carrying VMware drivers.

mac.description: Empty derives a stable MAC from the VM ID and the interface index (protocol.DerivedMAC: the 52:54:00 locally administered prefix, two octets of sha256(id) and the index), which never collides across a VM's at most 8 interfaces. A manual address must be six octets in canonical lower-case colon form and unicast; the pattern encodes the cleared multicast bit as an even second hex digit. All-zero addresses are refused, addresses are unique within the VM, and Controller additionally enforces uniqueness across the pool by plain string comparison. The VM list reports the effective address, and an edit freezes every automatic address into the definition (drawn from the VM's derived range above the highest index the VM uses, or the lowest free index when none above is free), so interfaces keep their identity across later edits.

mtu.description: Interface MTU, or 0 for the network's own. Accepted only when model is virtio: QEMU communicates an MTU to the guest through virtio's host_mtu feature and libvirt sizes the host tap to match, while the emulated models have no equivalent and would leave the guest on its own default. A value on any other model is refused rather than silently applied to the host side only. The floor is the IPv6 minimum MTU and the ceiling the largest jumbo frame common NICs accept; every device along the path must agree or traffic is dropped without an error.

VMNIC.description: One virtual network interface on a registered pool network. A VM may have none and at most 8.

firmware.description: uefi is the default and requires EFI firmware advertised by the host's libvirt domain capabilities; bios stays selectable.

machine.description: Empty selects Core's default machine type (q35).

media_boot_order.description: 0 keeps the CD drive out of the boot order; any other value joins the disks' contiguous 1..N numbering. Every VM has the drive, so the order is kept while it is empty and an ISO can be ejected from a running guest.

secure_boot.description: UEFI Secure Boot. Omitted means on with the Microsoft keys enrolled, which is exactly what libvirt already selected for every UEFI VM defined before this field existed, so a definition re-sent unchanged keeps the firmware its guest was installed with. off selects the plain OVMF build with no enrolled keys, for unsigned boot media or drivers. Requires uefi; on with bios is rejected. Core refuses the VM when the host's domain capabilities do not offer a matching firmware build, naming the setting rather than passing libvirt's firmware-selection error through. Changing it requires the VM to be shut off.

tpm.description: Emulated TPM. 2.0 adds a tpm-crb device backed by swtpm; omitted and none add no device, so a definition written before this field keeps exactly the devices it had. Windows 11 requires a TPM and refuses to install without one. Core refuses the VM when the host's domain capabilities do not advertise the emulator backend, rather than defining a device that cannot start. Changing it requires the VM to be shut off, and REMOVING a TPM is refused outright at any time: anything the guest sealed to it, including a Windows BitLocker key, would be lost, and libvirt cleans TPM state by iterating the devices the persistent definition still carries, so a redefine without it would orphan that state.

VMBoot.description: Firmware, Secure Boot, TPM, machine type and the install media's place in the boot order. Boot order is per device (libvirt forbids mixing per-device boot with an os/boot device list), so at least one disk or the install media must carry a non-zero order.

id.description: Controller-assigned stable UUID; identity is preserved across Controller replacement and later migration.

name.description: Nonblank VM name, at most 200 UTF-8 bytes (the byte limit is additionally enforced by Controller and Core). Spaces, case, dots, punctuation and Unicode are preserved exactly. Slashes, control characters and XML-invalid U+FFFE/U+FFFF are rejected. Core checks uniqueness on the host, journals the name and reports it for Controller adoption; failed or uncertain creations retain their reservation. Upgrade Controller and Core together to use the expanded naming syntax.

description.description: Free-text operator note, at most 4096 characters.

guest_os.description: Guest OS hint recorded for display and guest-tools advice; empty leaves it unset. It installs nothing and does not change the VM devices: disk bus and NIC model are chosen per device.

disks.description: One to eight disks; names unique within the VM.

media_id.description: Install ISO (Media.id), empty for none. The ISO must be imported and verified on the placement host; it may live on any storage that host can read and does not need to share a repository with the VM's disks. Every VM has the CD drive, so a non-zero boot.media_boot_order does not require media_id: an emptied drive keeps its place in the boot order.

drivers_media_id.description: ISO in the VM's second CD drive, for a driver disc an installer needs alongside its install media - a Windows guest installing to a VirtIO disk needs the virtio-win ISO here. Empty leaves that drive empty; the drive itself always exists on a host reporting vm-media-drivers-drive-v1. Must differ from media_id.

start_after_create.description: Honoured by the host inside the creation, after the definition is verified, so the creation itself has succeeded whether or not the flag is set: Core starts the guest exactly once and records the outcome in the journal entry's start field. A failed automatic start leaves the VM defined and stopped as a normal managed VM (power, console and media work; a replacement Controller adopts it) and is reported by the host as its own outcome with ID <operation-id>:start, kind vm-power, status failed and error 'VM created but not started: <reason>', which Controller records in Task history. A creation interrupted at the start step reconciles by observing libvirt: running means started, otherwise that outcome reads 'interrupted before the automatic start completed'. A failed or uncertain creation never boots. Controller issues no follow-on power request. Must be false in an edit.

autostart.description: libvirt autostart, set while the stopped guest is defined so the host starts this VM on boot. It is not a start.

tags.description: Operator labels kept with the VM definition: each 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, at most 16. Controller sorts and de-duplicates them before validation; an invalid tag is 400 naming it (tag "<tag>" must be 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens), more than 16 distinct tags is 400 (a VM allows at most 16 tags). Tags are part of the complete definition, so an edit that omits them clears them. Nonempty tags need vm-tags-v1 on both the VM's host and its pool master, because an older Core would drop them: 409 "the VM's host or its pool master does not support VM tags; upgrade Nex Core" on updateVM and "the selected host or its pool master does not support VM tags; upgrade Nex Core" on createVM, after the replay check. Core journals them with the definition, the pool master keeps them in its pool VM record, and a fresh Controller adopts them from the host's reported definition. Omitted when empty and from older Core. They change no guest device and apply to a running VM. Introduced in development product 0.4.8.

revision.description: Definition revision: 0 at creation, current + 1 for each edit. Core refuses any other value, so a stale edit after Controller replacement fails instead of applying an old definition. Reported back in Inventory.managed.vms with the current definition.

VMCreateSpec.description: The complete VM specification: Controller-assigned UUID and pool membership with separate host assignment, identity, CPU, memory, every disk and network interface, boot and install media, and the two lifecycle switches. Creation defines a stopped VM and never boots it. Dependencies must have succeeded on this host and pool. Both sides validate the shared bounds through protocol.ValidateVMSpec; Controller owns identity, reference existence, pool-wide MAC uniqueness and capacity.

StorageRegistrationRequest.description: A path-only body remains the protocol-v1 local-directory registration. Typed v2 repositories select kind and exactly one source. Core allocates the repository ID, canonicalizes identity and rechecks access before use.

StorageRegistrationIntent.description: Desired source configuration for a repository update. Core-owned ID, pool, host, operation status, identity, generation and observations are omitted; Core preserves its repository identity and validates the supplied intent.

NetworkLifecycleAPIRequest.description: Body of DELETE and PATCH /api/v1/networks/{id}. There is deliberately no host_id: the pool master owns pool VLANs and Controller resolves it, so a client-supplied host is rejected as an unknown field.

request_id.description: Stable idempotency key. The same key with the same body replays the original operation; with a different body it is 409.

expected_generation.description: The network generation the operator acted on. It must equal the mirrored registration's generation, so a stale view is refused instead of changing a network that moved underneath it.

name.description: PATCH only: the new network name.

MediaRemoveAPIRequest.description: Body of DELETE /api/v1/media/{id} for an import whose operation succeeded. The failed-import discard takes no body at all, and no pool, host or generation is accepted here: all three come from the host-reported record.

ResourceLifecycleResponse.description: Acceptance of a pool network or ISO lifecycle request. The resource stays in Controller's projection until the owning host reports the tombstone or the new name.

registration_request_id.description: For a backup registration use backup-credential:<kind>:<registration request_id>; the addressed host must be the pool master.

repository_id.description: Required for a backup-purpose offer; binds the receipt to one repository.

credentials.description: Transient material. Backup purpose accepts username plus secret for SMB3/S3, or username plus ssh_private_key for SFTP; no domain or ssh_known_hosts.

repository.description: Required for a backup-purpose offer: the destination the registration will submit. Controller refuses (400) a destination Core would refuse before offering the secret.

source.description: kind bridge/network only: existing bridge or active libvirt network name. Omit for kind vlan; Controller derives the bridge name <uplink>v<vlan>.

uplink.description: kind vlan only: host NIC or bond name that carries the VLAN, at most 10 characters; it must appear in the host inventory as physical or bond (or without a kind from an older agent).

vlan.description: kind vlan only: 802.1Q tag; 0 uses the uplink untagged, which Core refuses when the host has addresses on it.

NetworkRegistrationRequest.description: Exactly one shape: kind bridge/network with source, or kind vlan with uplink and vlan. Mixed fields are rejected with 400.

id.description: Omit; Controller generates the VM UUID.

warnings.description: Advisory only, omitted entirely when empty. One entry per required pool-shared repository, network or ISO whose access on the selected host this Controller's mirror does not currently show as current: "the pool master's last report does not show this host's access to <kind> <id> as current; the request may sit dispatched until it does", where <kind> is "storage repository", "network" or "ISO". It never changes the status, never refuses and is never stored; the pool master remains the placement authority and may well accept a request warned about here.

storage.description: Succeeded storage registrations from the host journal.

networks.description: Succeeded network registrations from the host journal.

media.description: Succeeded ISO imports from the host journal.

vms.description: Current VM definitions from the host journal: for each VM this host holds, the highest succeeded revision (creation is revision 0, each vm-update one more, and vm-media changes update the current entry), which is what a replaced Controller re-adopts by resource ID and what an existing Controller refreshes its mirror from on every report.

missing_vms.description: IDs of entries in vms whose persistent domain libvirt no longer lists (for example after an out-of-band undefine). The journal still holds them; Controller records each as a needs_attention operation instead of adopting it, and the host's managed-vms check reports failed. Omitted when libvirt lists every VM or cannot answer.

deleted_vms.description: Intentional VM deletions from succeeded vm-delete journal entries. Controller deletes its vm-create mirror for each tombstone. Distinct from missing_vms (accidental undefine while the journal still expects the VM).

appliances.description: Controller appliance VMs this host deployed through its local appliance engine, from that engine's deploy journal. Controller rebuilds its appliances record from them (insert when missing, keyed by VM UUID; moved to the reporting host when the previous owner is revoked) once healthy libvirt observes the VM, so a replaced Controller lists the appliance as the protected Controller VM again.

outcomes.description: Queued commands and terminal managed-journal outcomes, plus failed automatic-start results under <operation-id>:start. Orphaned non-storage work remains needs_attention. Core's serialized periodic lane retries at most one due pending/needs_attention storage-* original journal entry per minute, retains its original result and excludes definitive failures. Exact Core outcomes update matching nonterminal Controller operations; a replacement Controller adopts unknown operations as passive rows (actor system, request_id adopt-outcome:<host>:<operation_id>) and never redispatches them. The maximum covers 10000 execution journal entries, 10000 derived start results and 10000 additional retained agent commands; duplicate operation IDs are removed by Core.

credential_receipts.description: Redacted Core-owned storage and backup receipt metadata for adoption; it never contains credential bytes. Backup handoffs remain in the pool master's private Core state and are reported as cleanup eligible only without repository or unresolved registration references.

zfs_provisions.description: Core-owned ZFS provisioning results for Controller adoption.

recovery_reservations.description: Reported only by the pool master. Its durable unresolved snapshot operations, adopted by a fresh Controller as host observation; members omit it. Bounded by the 1 MiB pool authority limit.

recovery_reservations_reported.description: True only when the pool master successfully read and reported its durable snapshot reservation list; false or omitted is unknown, never an empty list.

join.description: This host's own durable staged pool join, reported while one is in progress and retained by the Controller alongside membership, so a fresh or restarted Controller adopts an interrupted join rather than losing it.

replica.description: This member's own stored copy of the pool master's signed authority, reported so an operator can see what would be recoverable. It is reported, never acted on; the master reports no replica for itself.

transfer.description: This host's own part of a pool master change or eject, reported by every participant so the Controller can assemble one honest picture from several hosts instead of keeping a job of its own. Its optional automatic flag is true only for the supported Core-started two-host BMC promotion; older Core versions omit the flag, which reads as false. Host fencing must be enabled. It is metadata, not fence proof; storage lease and qdevice witness do not trigger automatic promotion.

authority.description: Reported by the pool master only: its own durable authority generation and the digest of the content that generation numbered, so a member's acknowledged replica generation has an absolute reference to be compared against.

promotion.description: Reported by a promotion candidate only: its own fence-verified promotion of itself to pool master, with the stage it has durably reached and the last verdict it computed. The Controller mirrors it and records no candidate, stage or verdict of its own. Its optional automatic flag is true only for the supported Core-started two-host BMC promotion; older Core versions omit the flag, which reads as false. Host fencing must be enabled. It is metadata, not fence proof; storage lease and qdevice witness do not trigger automatic promotion.

restricted.description: This host's own Core-enforced refusal to act on pool authority, reported by whichever host holds it. It is a host report like any other: a restricted old master reports it for itself, which is how an operator sees that it came back and is starting nothing.

peer_origin.description: This host's own pool-peer origin as it works it out at report time from its configured peer listener (bind address, or the management address behind its default route, plus port): what a pool master would dial to reach it. An observation for the join dialog to prefill, mirrored by the Controller for display only; the join records the member's peer origin durably on the master. Omitted when the host has no route to work it out.

pool_vm_snapshots.description: Complete compact snapshot catalog reported only by the current pool master; host paths and native metadata are not included.

pool_vm_snapshots_reported.description: True only when the current pool master successfully loaded and reported the full catalog; false or omitted is unknown, not an empty catalog.

backup_repositories.description: Master-owned backup destinations (NFS, SMB3, S3 and SFTP) reported only by the current pool master.

backup_repositories_reported.description: True only when the master successfully loaded and reported the repository list; false or omitted is unknown, not empty.

iso_downloads.description: Live Core-observed byte counts for active URL ISO imports only, sent after Controller acknowledgement. Omitted after completion or interruption. Controller retains the latest report under the host inventory; display it as live only while the host connection is fresh.

detected_os.description: VM UUID to durable last detected OS, reported by the pool master from its Core-owned VM records. Optional; missing history does not mean the configured OS is a detected identity. Sent only after Controller acknowledgement of detected-os-v1.

update_rollout.description: The pool master's durable rollout record, reported by the master only and withheld until the Controller acknowledges image-update-v1.

ManagedState.description: Every succeeded registration and VM definition from the Core managed journal, plus the host's appliance deployments, queued work and terminal outcomes; at most 10000 entries per resource list and 30000 outcomes; each list is omitted when empty. Pool, host and resource IDs inside entries are host-owned and stable across Controllers: a host's self-registered default entry carries its pool ID when the host knows it (hosts enrolled with host-owned identity), otherwise its host ID as a placeholder until adoption. Adoption records each entry under the host's current pool and host, which is a no-op for hosts that presented their own identity at enrollment; that is how a replaced Controller recovers a pool from its master. Entries the Controller already holds under the same ID and kind are silently current. Any other entry it cannot adopt (invalid, conflicting ID/path/source/name, references not adopted on the host, or missing from libvirt) is recorded once per host and entry as a needs_attention operation (request_id adopt-attention:<host>:<kind>:<id>, actor system, error prefixed 'not adopted from host report:') with an audit entry adopt.attention naming the reason; the record is marked succeeded once the entry is adopted. A vm-create entry interrupted after its definition step is re-observed by the host on report and promoted to succeeded when the persistent domain matches its journaled definition.

token.description: Single-use pairing secret; the host presents it on POST /api/v1/agent/console/{token} within the ticket lifetime.

vm_id.description: VM UUID; omit or empty for the host console.

websocket.description: Same-origin path for the wss:// console stream; carries the ticket.

after_operation_id.description: Optional earlier same-VM task which Core must find succeeded in its managed journal before effects. Never the current operation ID. Sent only to vm-power-queue-v1 hosts; persisted with the command. Core also records a local prerequisite for a new power request admitted behind pending same-VM work.

request_id.description: Nonblank after trimming whitespace; at most 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR, LF, or NUL. Persist before sending; the same id replays the same operation.

interface.description: Guest interface name as reported by the guest agent; maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes.

address.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address in CIDR form. Loopback and link-local addresses are omitted.

agent.description: connected: the QEMU guest agent answered; unresponsive: the org.qemu.guest_agent.0 channel is attached but the agent did not answer within 1 second; disconnected: nothing in the guest has opened the channel; no-channel: the VM definition lacks the channel.

os.description: guest-get-osinfo pretty name; absent unless agent is connected. Maximum 4096 UTF-8 bytes.

os_id.description: guest-get-osinfo id: the guest's POSIX os-release ID (for example debian or ubuntu), or mswindows on Windows. Guest-reported and optional; maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes.

hostname.description: guest-get-host-name; absent unless agent is connected. Maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes.

addresses.description: guest-network-get-interfaces addresses without loopback or link-local entries; at most 32.

clipboard.description: ready: the guest opened the qemu-vdagent channel (spice-vdagent is running) so the console clipboard works both ways; waiting: the channel exists but nothing in the guest opened it; no-channel: the VM was defined before console clipboard support and must be recreated to gain it.

resize.description: True only when the guest can actually follow a console resize request: the VM has a VirtIO display and the guest has opened the qemu-vdagent channel, which is the agent that applies the new resolution. A VirtIO display alone only means the host would send the request; a guest without the driver ignores it (BUG-0201).

media.description: The live CD drive of the running VM: loaded when its tray holds media, empty when the drive holds none (a guest can eject its own disc, for example an installer after the base system), no-drive when the VM has no CD drive. Absent from Core builds that do not observe it. It reports what the guest sees; the durable media_id changes only through a media request.

drivers_media.description: The same live observation as media, for the VM's second (driver disc) CD drive. Absent from Core builds that define only one CD drive.

GuestInfo.description: Observed inside a running VM by its host through host-local virtio channels: guest agent facts and console channel states. Observation only; a connected agent is not proof of application health.

drive.description: Which of the VM's two CD drives the request applies to: install (or omitted, which is what every Controller sent before the second drive existed) or drivers.
