Core resolves the drive through libvirt user aliases, so the target letters libvirt assigns never matter. A Controller must not send drivers to a host that does not report vm-media-drivers-drive-v1.

media_id.description: ISO media ID already imported on the assigned host. Required for insert; omitted for eject.

id.description: Lowercase libvirt domain UUID of the appliance VM.

request_id.description: The deployment's stable request ID, which is also the request_id of POST /api/v1/appliances/adopt during the handoff.

Appliance.description: A Controller appliance VM the host deployed through its local appliance engine and still owns, reported from that engine's deploy journal (the host's durable ownership record).

operation_id.description: The host journal's operation ID: the Controller operation ID when this Controller issued it; <operation-id>:start for the automatic start of a vm-create entry.

id.description: Resource ID the operation addressed (registration, media or VM ID).

ManagedOutcome.description: Host-owned queued work and retained task outcomes. A replacement Controller adopts these passively, follows terminal status, and never redispatches them. Core retains admission order through restart and reenrollment.

id.description: Omit, or the VM UUID from the path.

pool_id.description: Must equal the VM's pool; editing never moves a VM.

host_id.description: Must equal the VM's assigned host; editing never moves a VM.

name.description: Nonblank VM name, at most 200 UTF-8 bytes (the byte limit is additionally enforced by Controller and Core). Spaces, case, dots, punctuation and Unicode are preserved exactly. Slashes, control characters and XML-invalid U+FFFE/U+FFFF are rejected. Core checks uniqueness on the host, journals the name and reports it for Controller adoption; failed or uncertain creations retain their reservation. Upgrade Controller and Core together to use the expanded naming syntax.

description.description: Free-text operator note, at most 4096 characters.

guest_os.description: Guest OS hint recorded for display and guest-tools advice; empty leaves it unset. It installs nothing and does not change the VM devices: disk bus and NIC model are chosen per device.

disks.description: One to eight disks; names unique within the VM.

media_id.description: Install ISO (Media.id), empty for none. The ISO must be imported and verified on the placement host; it may live on any storage that host can read and does not need to share a repository with the VM's disks. Every VM has the CD drive, so a non-zero boot.media_boot_order does not require media_id: an emptied drive keeps its place in the boot order.

start_after_create.description: Must be false; use the power controls to start a VM.

autostart.description: libvirt autostart, set while the stopped guest is defined so the host starts this VM on boot. It is not a start.

tags.description: Operator labels kept with the VM definition: each 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, at most 16. Controller sorts and de-duplicates them before validation; an invalid tag is 400 naming it (tag "<tag>" must be 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens), more than 16 distinct tags is 400 (a VM allows at most 16 tags). Tags are part of the complete definition, so an edit that omits them clears them. Nonempty tags need vm-tags-v1 on both the VM's host and its pool master, because an older Core would drop them: 409 "the VM's host or its pool master does not support VM tags; upgrade Nex Core" on updateVM and "the selected host or its pool master does not support VM tags; upgrade Nex Core" on createVM, after the replay check. Core journals them with the definition, the pool master keeps them in its pool VM record, and a fresh Controller adopts them from the host's reported definition. Omitted when empty and from older Core. They change no guest device and apply to a running VM. Introduced in development product 0.4.8.

UpdateVMRequest.description: The complete desired definition of an existing VM plus a stable request_id. Disks are matched to the current definition by name (storage, size and provisioning of an existing disk cannot change); interfaces by MAC, so send existing interfaces with the address the VM list reports and leave mac empty only for new ones. Controller answers 400 when an interface at an existing index has an empty mac and the request removes an interface or that interface's network, model or MTU differs from the current interface at that index; an unchanged interface or one appended past the current count may still omit it. Changing an existing interface's MAC is treated as removing that interface and adding a new one, which a running VM accepts.

request_id.description: Nonblank after trimming whitespace; at most 200 UTF-8 bytes; no CR, LF, or NUL. Persist before sending; the same id replays the same operation.

delete_disks.description: When true, Core unlinks the guest disk files after undefine. When false (default), files stay on storage and are recorded as retained.

VMTombstone.description: Intentional vm-delete tombstone from Core so Controller drops its mirror. Not the same as missing_vms.

token.description: Stats channel secret for this host; the host presents it on POST /api/v1/agent/stats/{token}.

StatsTier.description: Not serialized. Range-to-resolution table shared by Core and Controller: 10m = 5 s × 120, 24h = 1 min × 1440, 30d = 1 h × 720, 1y = 1 day × 365.

key.description: Stable series key, e.g. cpu.total, cpu.vcpu.0, cpu.core.3, memory.assigned, memory.host, memory.guest_used, memory.used, memory.total, disk.vda.read_bytes, disk.vda.write_iops, net.0.rx, net.eno1.tx, load.1. Keys ending .total are aggregates. Host temperature keys are temp.<chip>-<device>.<n>, built from the hwmon chip name and the sensor device, never the kernel's hwmon index.

values.description: One entry per step from start; null is unknown or not running, never zero. Exactly the range's point count (live and 10m 120, 24h 1440, 30d 720, 1y 365); the Controller relay answers 502 for a reply with any other length.

host_id.description: Host that holds this history; set by the Controller relay.

start.description: Time of values[0], aligned to a step boundary.

StatsHistory.description: Usage history kept on the host in fixed-size round-robin files under the agent state directory. The Controller keeps no copy.

CPUFeature.description: Native CPU feature policy. Names must be unique within one CPU definition; no guest-OS feature policy is inferred.

features.description: Optional fixed native CPU feature list. Omitted or empty retains model-only behavior. Nonempty requires a named model (not host modes or max) and vm-cpu-baseline-v1. Duplicate feature names are rejected.

CPUBaseline.description: Disposable Core-master observation for every current non-ejected ready pool member, including a single-host pool. Native baseline and exact destination comparisons must succeed under unchanged membership. Errors or absent observations are unavailable, never an inferred smaller pool. Saved VM definitions are independent; future members and live migration are not certified.

PoolWrappedKey.description: The pool CA private key sealed for exactly one member of one generation: ECDH between a fresh ephemeral P-256 key and that member's certified peer public key, HKDF-SHA256 with a context binding pool ID, member host ID and generation, then AES-256-GCM with the same context as additional data. A member stores it sealed and never opens it while it is a member; nothing in this release unwraps it. All three fields are standard base64.

ephemeral_public_key.description: Base64 uncompressed P-256 point of the master's per-push ephemeral key.

nonce.description: Base64 12-byte AES-GCM nonce, fresh for every push.

ciphertext.description: Base64 AES-256-GCM ciphertext of the pool CA private key PEM.

PoolReplicaSection.description: One declared section of an authority replica and the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON. A member recomputes every digest and refuses a replica that declares a different set, so a section cannot be dropped, reordered or replaced.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of that section's canonical JSON.

PoolAuthorityReplica.description: The pool master's signed, read-only copy of its own durable pool authority, pushed to one member. It is stored by every ready member and acted on by none of them: no membership, VM, storage, network, media or in-progress resource mutation on the receiving host is read from or changed by a replica, and no health judgement is derived from one. The signature is made with the pool CA key over every field but signature, so a member verifies it against the pool CA it pinned at join, long after the master that signed it is gone. Bounded to 1 MiB on the wire and on disk.

generation.description: The master's authority generation, which it advances only when the replicated content digest changes. Never 0 in a valid replica; generations may skip.

member_host_id.description: The one member this copy is addressed to. It is inside the signature, so a replica cannot be re-addressed in transit and a copy wrapped for one member cannot be presented to another.

vms.description: The master's pool-vms.json owner projection, replicated as received bytes so ownership, epochs, specs and pending updates survive unchanged. Published per-host inventory snapshots are deliberately not replicated: they are observations, and a promoted master re-collects fresh ones.

storage.description: Pool storage registrations with credential receipts stripped, exactly as the storage peer list strips them.

fence_credentials.description: The pool's fence credential material, sealed for this member alone. Like ca_key_wrapped it is covered by signature and excluded from the content digest, so one generation still has one digest for every member; what makes new material advance the generation is fence_credential_version in the membership.

sections.description: Exactly the seven sections above, in order.

signature.description: Base64 ASN.1 ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 signature by the pool CA key over the whole replica with signature empty.

witness_credentials.description: Per-member sealed native qdevice credentials. The shared qdevice key is wrapped separately to each member and bound to the fencing generation.

resource_mutations.description: In-progress destructive network or media removals, replicated so promotion cannot forget an unresolved outcome.

backup_manifest.description: Paged backup authority reference; the pages are pushed separately and bound by the manifest root.

corosync_key_wrapped.description: Pool Corosync authentication key sealed for this member and replica generation; required when the pool forms its own cluster.

update_rollout.description: The master's pool-update.json, declared as the section update_rollout only while a record exists (a pool that never rolled out keeps the older section layout). A promoted master adopts an active rollout paused master_changed.

PoolReplicaAck.description: The member's answer to one push. Re-pushing the same generation with the same content returns the same acknowledgement; a refusal carries a bounded reason and a 409, never a silent drop.

host_id.description: The acknowledging member. Empty in a refusal that could not be attributed.

digest.description: Content digest of the stored replica: identical on every member of one generation, because the per-member address, the per-push wrap, the creation time, the signature and the generation are excluded from it.

verified.description: True only when the replica was verified against the pool CA, its sections recomputed, and the file durably written.

sanlock_host_generation.description: Native host generation in the configured authority lockspace after this member joined it; absent or zero means no sanlock preparation acknowledgement.

corosync_key_ready.description: True only after the addressed Corosync key was opened and durably stored; required by the master for a pool cluster replica.

error.description: Bounded refusal reason; control characters collapse the whole message to "pool authority replica refused".

PoolReplicaStatus.description: Observed replica state, reported in a member's inventory.managed.replica and returned by the peer GET. It is what a host holds and how fresh that observation is; the Controller mirrors it for display and stores none of it.

generation.description: 0 when this host holds no replica.

received_at.description: When this host stored it, from the host's own clock, so freshness survives a restart.

error.description: The last refusal this host recorded, kept alongside whatever it still holds; a later accepted push clears it. Includes "pool member refused backup authority page reuse" when a reusable blob cannot be safely staged.

PoolMaintenanceRequest.description: Body of POST /api/v1/pools/{id}/members/{host_id}/maintenance. There is no confirmation field: draining a host stops nothing that is running, so there is nothing to confirm against. The guest list the operator should see before draining is returned by GET /api/v1/pools/{id}/members.

request_id.description: Client idempotency key. Persist it before sending: an exact retry returns the original operation with 200, and the same key with a changed payload conflicts.

enabled.description: Desired drain state, not a transition.

expected_version.description: The membership generation the operator saw; 0 or absent skips the check. The Controller compares it with the master's last reported generation and Core compares it again with the master's own.

PoolMaintenanceAccepted.description: Acceptance of a maintenance request. Acceptance is not the drain: the flag is set by the pool master when it collects the command, and the outcome is visible in the operation and in the member projection.

host_id.description: The host being drained, not the host the command is addressed to.

PoolMemberGuests.description: The member's own reported guest list, for the dialog an operator sees before draining. A host that is not reporting has no guest list: known is false and the client must show unknown, never none.

known.description: False whenever that host's connection is not fresh.

names.description: Capped at 50 names; total and running count them all.

PoolMemberOperation.description: The newest Controller-held operation of one kind for this member or host, so an asynchronous Core refusal is visible where the operator acted. Used by the pool members projection and by GET /api/v1/hosts/{id}/network.

conflict.description: True when a failed result carries one of the master's membership-conflict refusals ("pool membership changed since this request was composed; review the pool and try again", "pool membership is unavailable"). This is the 409 class for a durable asynchronous command: Core's refusal is never an HTTP status of the submitting route. For a management-network operation it is true when Core's failure text ends with "management network conflict".

PoolMemberReplica.description: One member's authority replica as the two hosts that report it describe it: the member says what it holds, the master says what it last saw acknowledged. Neither number is derived, stored or reconciled by the Controller, and no host reports an absolute pool authority generation, so there is no third number to compare against. null on the pool master's own row: the master holds the authority, not a replica of it.

generation.description: The member's own report; 0 when it holds none or is not fresh.

verified.description: The member proved the replica against the pool CA it holds.

acknowledged_generation.description: What the master last observed this member acknowledge; 0 when the master is not fresh or the member never acknowledged one.

error.description: The master's reason for this member when it has one, otherwise the member's own reported reason.

state.description: First match wins, in this order: unknown when the master is not fresh or this member is not fresh (a replica that was current an hour ago is not current now); refused when either side reports an error; awaiting when both generations are 0; unverified when the member holds a replica it has not proven; behind when the two generations disagree, the pool master reports an authority generation one of them is below, or another fresh member of this pool is acknowledged at a strictly higher generation; current otherwise. behind with generation above acknowledged_generation means the master's observation lags, not the member: both numbers are shown because the single word cannot say which side is stale. The pool master's reported authority generation is the absolute reference this ladder gained with the master change slice; the peer comparison stays, because the master's authority record can itself be an older report than a member's. When authority is null the ladder behaves exactly as it did before. Without a fresh master the ladder stops at what the member alone proves — refused, unverified, awaiting, otherwise unknown: current and behind are claims about a number only the master reports, and a member's own copy cannot stand in for it.

ManagementNIC.description: One interface of a host's management network configuration. Name is the on-host interface name the host already has (the installer's nexN); renaming an interface is not part of a staged change, because /etc/systemd/network/*.link only takes effect on boot and could not be undone inside a rollback window.

name.description: Existing on-host interface name: first character a letter, then letters, digits, - or _.

mac.description: Unicast MAC of that interface, aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff. It binds the rendered configuration to the hardware.

mode.description: disabled carries no address, gateway, VLAN or management role; dhcp carries no address or gateway.

vlan.description: VLAN tag for the management VLAN on this interface; absent or 0 for untagged.

address.description: IPv4 address with prefix, for example 192.0.2.10/24. Static mode only. A 1-32 prefix, not 0.0.0.0, not loopback, nothing from 224.0.0.0 up, and not the network or broadcast address outside a /31 or /32.

gateway.description: Default gateway, only on the management interface, inside its own subnet and not its own address.

management.description: Exactly one interface in a spec carries it. It becomes the br0 management bridge Nex Core renders.

ManagementNetworkSpec.description: The whole desired management network configuration of one host. Nex Core owns the rules: the wire only bounds it (1-64 interfaces, at most 8 DNS servers) and Core validates and renders it.

dns.description: IPv4 name servers. Nex Core writes /etc/resolv.conf when the management interface is static or these override DHCP.

ManagementNetworkStatus.description: The host's own report of its management network, projected from <state-dir>/management-network.json and the on-disk Nex-managed files into inventory.management_network. It is the only copy: a replaced Controller adopts an in-flight change, with its deadline, by reading this, and reads the live configuration as current even when no change has been staged.

revision.description: Incremented by a confirm, so expected_revision pins the configuration the operator saw.

stage.description: none when the host has no change record but may still report current; a record is never deleted, so the last outcome stays readable; rolled-back is what the host reports after an unconfirmed change was restored automatically.

operation_id.description: The change's own ID, which apply, confirm and cancel name as change_id.

spec.description: The staged, applied or confirmed configuration.

deadline.description: When an applied, unconfirmed change is restored by the host itself. Absent until the change is applied, and cleared by a confirm or a rollback.

window_seconds.description: The rollback window recorded when the change was staged, so "how long will I have" survives a page reload. Absent from a Core older than this field.

seconds_remaining.description: Time left at observed_at, reported only while the stage is applied. It is the host's own arithmetic, not the Controller's.

last_error.description: The reason the host recorded for the last rollback, or a failed apply.

requested_rollback.description: True when this rollback was the operator asking for it — a cancel submitted against an applied, unconfirmed change — rather than the host undoing an unconfirmed change at its deadline or after a reboot. It is durable, so a rollback interrupted before the previous configuration came back up resumes as the same operator rollback. The host emits no failing management-network health check for an operator rollback: it is an outcome, not a failure.

current.description: What the host's Nex-managed /etc files say right now. Independent of spec: spec is the staged, applied or last change; current is parsed from disk so a Controller can show live addressing before any change has been staged. Absent when the files are missing or were not written by Nex.

observed_gateway.description: Optional live default IPv4 gateway on br0, read from the host route table. Observed state only; absent if no gateway is reported. DHCP configuration specs still omit address and gateway.

ManagementNetworkRequest.description: One step of a staged management network edit, carried by the durable managed-command path so it survives a Controller outage.

operation_id.description: Equal to the command envelope's operation ID and unique per command: it is the managed journal's key, so a redelivered command replays its recorded result instead of acting twice.

host_id.description: The target host. The agent refuses a command addressed to another host.

change_id.description: The staged change this action targets: the operation_id the host recorded when it staged it. Required for apply, confirm and cancel; refused on stage, which creates the change and names it after its own operation_id.

spec.description: Required for stage, and carried as an object rather than null on every action: the field is a value in the Go type, so an apply, confirm or cancel sends it empty rather than omitting it.

expected_revision.description: The revision the operator saw; 0 skips the check. Staging against a stale revision is a conflict.

window_seconds.description: Rollback window for stage; 0 means the host's default of 600. The wire bounds it at 0-3600 and Core refuses anything outside 120-1800.

confirmation.description: Required for apply and checked by the host itself: it must equal the host's own hostname, trimmed and case-insensitive. A Controller mirror can be stale; the hostname cannot.

HostNetworkRequest.description: Body of POST /api/v1/hosts/{id}/network. Only the fields the action needs are sent; unknown fields are refused.

request_id.description: Client idempotency key. Persist it before sending: an exact retry of the same payload returns the original operation with 200, and the same key with a changed payload conflicts.

change_id.description: Optional on apply, confirm and cancel: the management_network.operation_id the client loaded from the GET. The Controller always takes the id it sends from the host's own latest report, never from its own memory, so a change_id naming a different change is a 409 rather than a silent retarget. Refused on stage.

spec.description: Required for stage: 1-64 interfaces, at most 8 DNS servers. Core validates the rest.

expected_revision.description: The revision the operator saw; 0 or absent skips the check. Compared with the host's last reported revision here, and again by Core against its own record.

window_seconds.description: Rollback window for stage; 0 or absent means the host's default of 600 seconds. This route only rejects values outside 0-3600; Core refuses anything outside 120-1800 as an asynchronous failure.

confirmation.description: Required for apply: the host's own reported hostname, typed by the operator. Checked here and again by the host.

HostNetworkAccepted.description: Acceptance of one step. Acceptance is not the change: the host performs it when it collects the command, and the outcome is visible in the operation and in GET /api/v1/hosts/{id}/network.

HostNetworkCheck.description: The host's own management-network health check, as reported in its inventory.

detail.description: The check's error text: Nex Core's rollback reason, or "the management network record is unreadable".

HostNetworkView.description: Everything GET /api/v1/hosts/{id}/network returns is a host report or this Controller's own operation history. The Controller keeps no management network state of its own.

hostname.description: The host's own reported hostname, falling back to the enrolled name before a first report. This is the string the operator must type to apply a change.

state.description: The record's stage, "none" when the host has never staged a change, and "unknown" whenever connection is not fresh. Losing contact during a countdown reads as unknown with the deadline still visible, never as success or failure.

management_network.description: The host's last reported record, null when it has never staged a change. It is returned even when the host is not fresh, because a running rollback deadline must stay readable; state says it is unknown.

nics.description: The host's own last reported interface inventory, which is what a spec is built from. [] when the host has never reported.

check.description: The host's management-network check, null when absent (absence means cleared) and null whenever connection is not fresh.

last_operation.description: The newest management-network operation this Controller holds for the host, or null. Its action is the submitted step, and conflict is true when Core's failure text ends with "management network conflict".

operation_id.description: The Controller operation that started the transfer, or the identifier the transfer was recorded under.

action.description: promote or eject: Core's own name for what this transfer does. A fence-verified promotion of a surviving member is also promote, and is told apart by role: candidate. The Controller's requested action (master-change, eject, transfer-cancel) is reported separately in last_transfer.

role.description: This host's part in the transfer: source is the pool master that started it, target is the host taking the authority, ejected is the host leaving the pool, candidate is the surviving member running a fence-verified promotion.

target_host_id.description: The transfer's subject: the host becoming master, or the host being ejected.

stage.description: The stage this host has durably reached. For a master change: freeze, replicate, activate (the signed hand-off), repoint (every other host is told, in the new master's own signed words, who the master is now). For an eject: freeze, remove (the durable membership change, after which nothing stays frozen), repoint, leave. For a promotion: preflight, fence, activate, optional catalog-rebuild (after authority commit when repositories exist and the signed catalog is empty), repoint. A catalog import error leaves catalog-rebuild at needs_attention for retry before repoint, without reactivating or rolling back the committed master. done and aborted are terminal.

status.description: pending while the hosts are still running it; needs_attention means durable and still running, not an error.

error.description: This host's own last refusal or failure, bounded and sanitized.

authority_generation.description: The pool authority generation this transfer is pinned to.

frozen.description: True while this host is refusing pool authority writes for the transfer. Running guests are unaffected and stop is never refused.

cancellable.description: Core's own answer to "may this still be cancelled?", so no caller has to infer it from stage names. True only before the transfer's first irreversible durable step: a master change until the pool-CA-signed hand-off, an eject until the membership without that member is written, and never for a promotion, which fences. It is computed from the same predicate the cancel itself is gated on, so the reported flag and the accepted cancel cannot drift. It is always present: a caller reads one field for every kind of transfer and never has to tell "not cancellable" from "not reported".

handed_off.description: The outgoing master's own durable answer to "have I signed this pool's authority away?", reported rather than inferred from stage names or refusal sentences. Only the source records it, so a target or ejected host always reports false. It is always present, so an older Core that omits it is distinguishable from one that reports false.

observed_at.description: When this host wrote this report.

automatic.description: True only when Core initiated this promotion automatically through the supported two-host BMC path. Omitted for manual promotions and by older Core versions. This is reported metadata, not a fence proof. Automatic promotion requires Host fencing enabled; storage-lease and witness-based promotion paths are not implemented; qdevice registration and status do not produce fence proof.

PoolTransferStatus.description: One participant's own report of the master change or eject it is part of. Every participant reports its own; nothing merges them into a job, and a host that is not reporting says nothing rather than repeating its last stage.

owner_operation_order.description: Nonzero durable owner command order for create, revert and delete; exact reservations and last settled receipts reject delayed older requests.

admission_refusal.description: A definitive no-effect snapshot-create refusal. It must settle only as failed-before-effects and cannot authorize native creation.

target_snapshot_id.description: Exact retained target ID; required only for revert.

target_snapshot_sha256.description: Canonical exact target descriptor hash; required only for revert.

result_spec_sha256.description: Master-derived expected restored VM specification hash; required only for revert.

PoolVMRecoveryReservation.description: Master-owned pending snapshot intent bound to exact owner/epoch, current VM/disk definition, native intent and operation order. Revert additionally binds the retained target descriptor and master-derived next specification; the master persists that pending result beside the reservation. Create admission_refusal is a definitive no-effect duplicate-name/full-catalog decision. Matching development Core versions are required.

snapshot.description: Required for completed snapshot-create evidence; absent on all other outcomes.

result_spec.description: Required only for completed revert; exact observed resulting VM specification must match the master-derived reservation hash. Absent on create and failed-before-effects.

PoolVMRecoveryEvidence.description: Owner-generated receipt for one exact terminal managed-journal record. Unknown, partial and failed-after-effects outcomes leave the reservation pending.

generation.description: The pool master's own durable authority generation. This is the only absolute generation in the pool; nothing else derives one.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the authority content that generation numbered.

PoolAuthorityRecord.description: Reported by the pool master alone. A Controller mirrors it to compare each member's acknowledged replica generation against it and stores neither.

from_host_id.description: The host that issued and signed this notice.

target_host_id.description: The transfer's subject: the promoted host, or the ejected one.

authority_generation.description: The exact authority generation being handed over, or the generation the issuing master holds.

signature.description: Base64 ASN.1 ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 over the whole notice minus this field, made with the pool CA key. Every recipient verifies it against the pool CA it pinned at join, so no host takes another host's word for who the master is.

PoolAuthorityNotice.description: The pool-CA-signed statement that pool authority moved. Used twice in one transfer: the hand-off, signed by the outgoing master, naming the exact generation it froze and the host it handed that generation to (membership empty); and the re-point, signed by the new master with the pool CA key it now holds, carrying the new membership at a strictly higher membership generation. A notice without a signature, or at a generation that is not strictly higher, is refused.

operation_id.description: Idempotency key: the same request repeated after a lost reply returns the same answer and performs the step at most once.

action.description: activate hands the authority to the addressed host; abort records that it never activated and never will for this operation; repoint moves the addressed host onto the new master; leave tells an ejected host it has left.

PoolTransferRequest.description: One step of a transfer, addressed to one peer. abort carries no meaningful notice; every other action requires one whose operation_id matches.

host_id.description: The host that answered.

activated.description: The fact an abort needs: whether this host had already adopted the authority, decided once under its own lock, so an abort and an activation can never both succeed.

authority_generation.description: This host's authority generation after the step.

membership_generation.description: This host's membership generation after the step.

notice.description: Returned with an accepted activation: the new master's own signed re-point notice, so the outgoing master demotes itself on signed evidence rather than on its assumption that the activation worked.

PoolTransferReply.description: The addressed host's own answer to one transfer step.

host_id.description: The host that answered the probe.

role.description: This host's own role in the pool it names.

master_host_id.description: The host this host currently follows as pool master.

master_peer_origin.description: That master's peer origin, so a converging host can go on to probe it.

authority_generation.description: This host's own pool authority generation; 0 on a member.

membership_generation.description: The membership generation this host holds.

replica_generation.description: The generation of the authority replica this host stores.

replica_verified.description: Whether that replica was proven against the pool CA.

frozen.description: This host is refusing pool authority writes for a transfer.

handed_off.description: This host has signed its authority away and refuses every authority write for good, not only while frozen.

caller_status.description: The membership status this host holds for the calling certificate, decided from the certificate the transport proved rather than from a name in a body. Empty when it names no member at all. This is how an ejected host learns it has been ejected.

transfer.description: This host's own part of a transfer.

notice.description: A master answers a ready member that is behind with a signed re-point notice, so a host that missed a push converges from whichever host it can reach without having to trust a stale one. The probe answer alone changes nothing; only the signature at a strictly higher generation does.

restricted.description: This host's own refusal to act on pool authority, set while it cannot prove it holds the pool's current authority. A returning fenced master answers its probes with this, which is how a member and an operator see that it came back and is refusing to start anything.

vms.description: This host's own view of the VM definitions it owns, answered only when the caller asks with ?vms=1. Consumed by the promotion proof of a later slice.

vms_reported.description: Separates "this host defines no VM" from "this host could not read its own record": an empty vms list means the first only when this is true.

PoolAuthorityStatus.description: The read-only authority probe every host answers to any holder of a certificate this pool's CA issued, including one this pool has ejected. It is how a returning or restarted host discovers that it has been superseded or ejected, and how a host that missed a re-point finds the current master without trusting a stale one.

host_id.description: The host that defines this VM, as that host itself reports it.

revision.description: The definition revision this host holds.

PoolVMOwnership.description: One host's own statement about one VM it defines, answered by the authority probe only when the caller asks for it. The execution epoch is deliberately absent: it is the master's number and a member could only repeat it back rather than confirm it. Consumed by the promotion proof of a later slice, which is not documented in this release.

kind.description: The structural form of reason, so no caller has to match on the sentence. unconfirmed is a master that has not re-proved its authority since it restarted; superseded is a host that found a higher authority elsewhere. Omitted by an older Core, in which case the sentence is the only signal.

reason.description: Why this host is refusing to act on pool authority.

conflicts.description: VMs this host still defines that the current pool master records as running elsewhere. A conflict is never resolved by guessing.

PoolRestrictedStatus.description: A Core-enforced refusal state on a host that cannot prove it holds the pool's current authority: while it is set the host writes no pool authority, mints no authority generation, starts no workload and autostarts nothing. Stop, power-off, console, local recovery access and reporting are untouched, and the libvirt hook refuses managed shared-VM starts by reading the host's own durable record, so the refusal holds with no Controller connected. It is reported by the authority probe, by inventory.managed.restricted and by GET /api/local/v1/pool.

request_id.description: Stable, operator-supplied idempotency key. The same request_id with a byte-identical payload returns the original operation and starts no second transfer; with any other payload it is refused.

host_id.description: The ready member that becomes the pool master.

expected_version.description: Optional. The membership generation the pool master last reported, as shown in GET /api/v1/pools/{id}/members. When it no longer matches, the request is refused and nothing is queued.

confirmation.description: The pool's name exactly as pool_name reports it, compared case-insensitively after trimming. A master change pauses every pool authority write until it completes, so the pool is typed by hand. Omitted from required because the Go request type omits it when empty; the route refuses the request with 400 when it does not match.

PoolMasterChangeRequest.description: Planned master change. Unknown fields are refused.

request_id.description: Stable, operator-supplied idempotency key. The same request_id with a byte-identical payload returns the original operation and starts no second transfer; with any other payload it is refused.

expected_version.description: Optional. The membership generation the pool master last reported, as shown in GET /api/v1/pools/{id}/members. When it no longer matches, the request is refused and nothing is queued.

confirmation.description: The ejected host's name exactly as members[].name reports it, compared case-insensitively after trimming. Omitted from required because the Go request type omits it when empty; the route refuses the request with 400 when it does not match.

PoolEjectRequest.description: Eject a member. The host is named by the path, not by the body. Unknown fields are refused.

request_id.description: Stable, operator-supplied idempotency key. The same request_id with a byte-identical payload returns the original operation and starts no second transfer; with any other payload it is refused.

host_id.description: The transfer's target, as transfer.target_host_id reports it. Core refuses a cancel that names another target.

expected_version.description: Optional. The membership generation the pool master last reported, as shown in GET /api/v1/pools/{id}/members. When it no longer matches, the request is refused and nothing is queued.

fence_confirmed.description: Optional, and confirmed together with fence_host_ids or not at all. The operator's explicit agreement to power the transfer's target off, which Core needs only when a handed-off target has stopped answering and this pool's authority would otherwise stay with a dead host. Core refuses it while the target is reachable.

fence_host_ids.description: Optional, and confirmed together with fence_confirmed or not at all. It names the transfer's target once and nothing else. Half a confirmation is refused with 400 "powering the transfer target off is confirmed with both fence_confirmed and fence_host_ids naming that host once, or with neither".

PoolTransferCancelRequest.description: Cancel a transfer that has not handed the authority over. There is no typed confirmation: a cancel is the undo, and after the hand-off Core refuses it anyway. Unknown fields are refused.

host_id.description: The request's subject: the new master, the ejected host, the cancelled transfer's target, the promotion candidate, or the host a fence profile belongs to. For a master change, an eject and a cancel this is not the host the command is addressed to, which is the current pool master; for a promotion it is, because a promotion is run by the candidate.

action.description: The action that was asked for.

PoolTransferAccepted.description: Acceptance of a transfer request. Acceptance is not the transfer: the pool master runs it and every participant reports its own stage in GET /api/v1/pools/{id}/members.

action.description: The action that was asked for, not Core's internal promote. In last_promotion it is always promote.

error.description: Core's own refusal or failure text, verbatim.

reason.description: Core's own sentence for an operation that succeeded, and empty otherwise. A fence-backed cancel is the case that needs it: Core reports the cancellation it performed as succeeded and says in the same breath what it did, which is an outcome an operator must read rather than a failure. error stays empty then, so a successful cancellation can never be rendered as a failed transfer.

conflict.description: This refusal is one a synchronous route would have answered with 409. The pool changed between composing the request and Core deciding it; reload before retrying.

retryable.description: Marks exactly one sentence — "pool authority is frozen for a master change; retry when it completes" — which an operator retries unchanged once the current transfer finishes.

PoolTransferOperation.description: The newest pool-transfer command this Controller relayed for the pool, so an asynchronous Core refusal is visible where the operator acted.

name.description: replica-integrity: this host holds a verified signed replica. replica-supremacy: no reachable host holds a newer pool authority. accepted-ownership: every pool VM is recorded the same way by the host that owns it. old-master-exclusion: the old pool master has been fenced and its power-off observed by Core itself.

status.description: unknown blocks a promotion exactly as blocked does. It is a different word only so an operator can tell a refusal from an outage, and it is never presented as "fine". old-master-exclusion is normally unknown before the promotion runs, because Core fences and proves it during the promotion and never during a preflight.

hosts.description: The hosts this check is about.

vms.description: The pool VMs this check is about.

PoolPromotionCheck.description: One named check of the promotion proof, computed on the candidate from its own replica and its own live probes.

reachable.description: Whether the candidate reached this host over the pool network. An unreachable host is reported unreachable, never assumed stopped.

role.description: master or member, as that host answered.

authority_generation.description: The pool authority generation that host answered with.

replica_generation.description: The replica generation that host holds.

membership_generation.description: The membership generation that host holds.

blocks.description: This host's own answer to "does this host stop the promotion as things stand": an unreachable member that could itself have been promoted, or a reachable one that disagrees. A blocking host that can be fenced appears in the verdict's fence_host_ids; one that cannot is a refusal an operator must resolve another way.

fence_recorded.description: Whether a fence profile is recorded for this host at all.

fence_usable.description: Whether the candidate could turn that profile into a proof for this host: a profile kind this build can verify, plus a credential sealed to the candidate that it can open.

fence_unusable_reason.description: Core's own short sentence when it could not.

fence_kind.description: The recorded fence profile's kind, so a caller can show which method this promotion would shut this host out with. Empty when no profile is recorded.

fence_check_warning.description: Advisory only: what this candidate's own last non-destructive check of that fence device found, when it was failing or stale. The promotion's proof path is unchanged and still decides; this exists so an operator is not surprised by a fence device that was already known to be unreachable.

error.description: The probe's own bounded failure text.

PoolPromotionHost.description: One probed host of the replica's membership, as the promotion candidate found it, with that host's own contribution to the verdict: whether it blocks the promotion, and whether the candidate could exclude it by a fence if it does.

host_id.description: The host the pool authority records as this VM's owner.

state.description: confirmed by its reachable owner, fenced with its owner, or blocked. A blocked VM does not block the pool's promotion; it stays visible and unstartable until it is reconciled, and its definition is never deleted.

reason.description: Core's own sentence for a blocked VM.

PoolPromotionVM.description: One VM record of the replica, classified by the candidate against what the owning host itself reports.

candidate_host_id.description: The surviving member this verdict is about: the host that would become master.

old_master_host_id.description: The pool master this promotion would exclude.

operation_id.description: The promotion this verdict was computed for, when it belongs to one.

authority_generation.description: The generation the candidate would promote from.

can_promote.description: True only when the whole proof holds right now, fence included. In the normal ready state it is false, because the old master has not been fenced yet: that is an honest "not proved", not a refusal. A caller must not use it alone to decide whether to offer the promotion.

ready_to_fence.description: The state a caller offers the operator the promotion in: every check but the exclusion has passed, the exclusion is unknown only because no fence has been attempted, and the candidate holds a usable fence profile and an openable credential for every host in fence_host_ids. Confirming now proceeds to the fence rather than to a refusal.

fence_required.description: Whether this promotion needs a fence proof at all.

fence_recorded.description: Whether the old pool master has a fence profile recorded in the membership at all.

fence_usable.description: Whether this host could turn that profile into a proof: a profile kind this build can verify, plus a credential sealed to this host that it can open. Only virsh profiles can be recorded by this build, so a physical pool reports false.

fence_unusable_reason.description: Core's own short single-line sentence when it could not: "no fence profile is recorded for <host>", "this host holds no fence credential for <host>", or vmhost.PoolFenceUsable's own sentence such as "this host does not report a unique hardware identity, so a management controller cannot be confirmed to be its own".

fence_host_ids.description: Every host this promotion would power off, sorted: the old pool master, and every other host that blocks the promotion and can be excluded by a fence. It is what the operator confirms and what the promotion command carries back verbatim, so a host is never powered off without having been named to the operator first.

checks.description: Every named check, in Core's order.

hosts.description: Every host of the replica's membership, as the candidate probed it.

vms.description: Every pool VM of the replica, classified.

fence.description: The fence proof Core produced, when one exists. Always absent from a preflight: a preflight fences nothing.

blocking.description: Every blocking sentence, so a caller can show what must change without matching on check names. can_promote is exactly "this list is empty".

observed_at.description: When the candidate computed this verdict. A verdict is an observation with a lifetime, not a record: it is recomputed, never stored.

PoolPromotionVerdict.description: The promotion candidate Core's whole structured answer, computed on Core from its own signed replica and its own live probes of the pool network. A preflight returns it without changing anything, so an operator sees exactly what blocks before confirming a destructive fence. Nothing in it is computed, cached or stored by the Controller.

stage.description: The stage the candidate has durably reached: preflight, fence, activate, optional catalog-rebuild, repoint, done or aborted. A failed catalog import remains at catalog-rebuild with needs_attention until Core retries it.

status.description: needs_attention means durable and still running on Core, not an error.

error.description: The candidate's own last refusal or failure, bounded and sanitized.

verdict.description: The last verdict this host computed for the promotion.

cancellable.description: Core's own answer to "may this still be cancelled?". A promotion fences the old master, so it is never true; it is reported rather than inferred so a caller reads one field for every kind of transfer. It is always present: a caller reads one field for every kind of transfer and never has to tell "not cancellable" from "not reported".

observed_at.description: When this host wrote this report.

automatic.description: True only when Core initiated this promotion automatically through the supported two-host BMC path. Omitted for manual promotions and by older Core versions. This is reported metadata, not a fence proof. Automatic promotion requires Host fencing enabled; storage-lease and witness-based promotion paths are not implemented; qdevice registration and status do not produce fence proof.

PoolPromotionStatus.description: The promotion candidate's own report of the fence-verified promotion it is running. Reported as inventory.managed.promotion; the Controller stores no stage, no candidate and no verdict.

host_id.description: The host this material fences.

credential_ref.description: Core's own opaque reference for the material. It names a file in the host's state directory and is never projected to a client.

version.description: The master's counter for the material, so a member can tell a re-wrap of the same material from new material. It is mirrored in PoolMember.fence_credential_version, which is what makes rotated material advance the pool authority generation.

wrapped.description: The material sealed for this member alone, by the same primitive and with the same guarantees as the pool CA key, under its own context binding pool, member, generation, fenced host and reference.

PoolWrappedFenceCredential.description: One host's fence credential material carried to one member inside that member's replica. The host that actually fences during a promotion is a surviving member, and it cannot be given the material after the master it must fence is gone, so the material travels sealed rather than not at all. A member stores it sealed in its 0600 replica and opens it only while it performs a promotion; the Controller never sees it, and it never reaches SQLite, the audit trail, a response or a log. Every ready member can open the material addressed to it, which is the same trust model the sealed pool CA key already carries: admit only hosts you trust with powering off a profiled host.

kind.description: The recorded profile kind: redfish, ipmilan or virsh. virsh is for a Nex Core running as a virtual machine in a disposable lab. Empty when no profile is recorded and the object carries only a management-controller report or an identity conflict.

endpoint.description: The recorded endpoint, for recognition only.

configured.description: True when a fence profile is recorded. False when this object carries only the host's management-controller report or an identity conflict.

credential_version.description: The pool master's own counter for the private material behind this profile, mirrored verbatim from PoolMember.fence_credential_version; 0 means no material is recorded. The material itself never reaches this Controller — the number is only what tells an operator that a rotation has actually been replicated.

username.description: The management-controller account the master recorded, mirrored verbatim so an operator can see which account a fence would use. Absent on a virsh profile. The password behind it never reaches this Controller.

tls_fingerprint.description: The certificate the pool master pinned when the profile was recorded, mirrored verbatim so an operator can compare it with the controller's own page. Absent on ipmilan and virsh profiles.

bmc.description: The host's own report about its own management controller, mirrored verbatim from the master's membership record. It is present on a host that has no profile at all — which is exactly the host whose row offers Set BMC access… instead — so this object is non-null whenever there is a profile, a controller report or an identity conflict to show.

system_uuid_conflict_host_id.description: The member that already reported the hardware identity this host reports, when the master refused this host's report because of it. Mirrored verbatim; this Controller records nothing.

provisioned_by_core.description: The account behind this profile is one the host's own Nex Core created on its controller, so clearing the profile also removes that account and stops this host configuring it again. Mirrored verbatim.

provisioning_disabled.description: The pool master's own recorded decision that this host must not configure its management controller for fencing, mirrored verbatim. Clearing a fence device Nex Core provisioned sets it. It is what the host row's actions are decided from, because a host that is down after its device was cleared has echoed nothing and the master's decision is the one that is true.

readiness.description: The pool master's own answer to whether this host could be shut out, per method. Reported only by the master, only for the membership it owns, and never written into the durable record. Absent from a Core too old to report it, which a Controller shows as "not reported" and never as ready.

watchdog.description: The host's own watchdog report, mirrored verbatim from the master's membership record. Null when the host never reported one, which is never counted.

watchdog_armed.description: That host's own report that it has armed its watchdog, recorded durably by the master. Null means the host never said, which is never a watchdog exclusion proof.

PoolMemberFence.description: What the pool master's membership records about how this host would be excluded. It is master-derived, so it is null while the master is not fresh, and it never carries the credential reference or anything the reference names. There is deliberately no usable field here: no host reports per member whether a profile could be turned into a proof, and the promotion preflight's fence_usable is the authority on that.

host_id.description: The host that reported this promotion. The Controller records no candidate: it shows the fresh host of this pool with the most recent promotion report.

stage.description: The stage the candidate has durably reached: preflight, fence, activate, optional catalog-rebuild, repoint, done or aborted. A failed catalog import remains at catalog-rebuild with needs_attention until Core retries it.

status.description: needs_attention means durable and still running on Core, not an error.

error.description: The candidate's own last refusal or failure, bounded and sanitized.

verdict.description: The last verdict this host computed for the promotion.

cancellable.description: Core's own answer to "may this still be cancelled?". A promotion fences the old master, so it is never true; it is reported rather than inferred so a caller reads one field for every kind of transfer. It is always present: a caller reads one field for every kind of transfer and never has to tell "not cancellable" from "not reported".

observed_at.description: When this host wrote this report.

automatic.description: True only when Core initiated this promotion automatically through the supported two-host BMC path. Omitted for manual promotions and by older Core versions. This is reported metadata, not a fence proof. Automatic promotion requires Host fencing enabled; storage-lease and witness-based promotion paths are not implemented; qdevice registration and status do not produce fence proof.

PoolPromotionView.description: A promotion candidate's own reported promotion, with the host that reported it. Not master-derived: it is shown while the pool master is stale or gone, which is the only time it matters.

host_id.description: The surviving member to ask. The pool master is deliberately not consulted: a preflight is exactly what an operator runs when it is gone.

PoolPromotionPreflightRequest.description: Ask one candidate what blocks its promotion. Unknown fields are refused.

PoolPromotionPreflightView.description: One brokered report round trip to the candidate. Nothing is stored, journalled or audited and no command is issued, so it is safe to call repeatedly.

request_id.description: Stable, operator-supplied idempotency key. The same request_id with a byte-identical payload returns the original operation; with any other payload it is refused.

host_id.description: The surviving member that becomes master. The command goes to it.

confirmation.description: The pool's name exactly as pool_name reports it, compared case-insensitively after trimming. Omitted from required because the Go request type omits it when empty; the route refuses the request with 400 when it does not match.

fence_confirmed.description: Must be literally true: the operator's separate, explicit acknowledgement that the hosts named in fence_host_ids will be powered off. A precondition only — Core still produces and verifies every fence proof itself. Omitted from required because the Go request type omits it when false; the route refuses the request with 400 when it is not true.

fence_host_ids.description: Required and non-empty: exactly the set the candidate's own fresh preflight named in verdict.fence_host_ids, each host listed once. The Controller computes, completes and corrects nothing; it sorts the set so the same confirmation typed in another order is a replay rather than a second promotion, and forwards it verbatim. Core recomputes the set when the promotion runs and refuses a promotion whose confirmation no longer matches, so no host is ever powered off without having been named to the operator first.

PoolPromoteRequest.description: Promote a surviving member after Core fences the old pool master and every other host that blocks the promotion. There is no expected_version: the generation to check against is the dead master's, and the candidate re-proves the whole verdict immediately before it activates. Unknown fields are refused.

request_id.description: Stable, operator-supplied idempotency key. The stored replay payload is the profile as sent, without the credential and without the reference Core allocates, so an exact retry stays byte-identical.

fence.description: The profile to record; null clears it. redfish and ipmilan take {endpoint, target_id, username}; virsh takes the pinned SSH fields. A client never supplies tls_fingerprint: for a redfish profile Core connects when it records it, captures the certificate the controller presents, writes that fingerprint into the profile itself and proves over that pinned connection that the controller manages this host's machine before recording anything. Before any power-off Core asks the management controller which machine it manages — the Redfish ComputerSystem.UUID, compared exactly, or IPMI Get System GUID, where either documented byte order counts — and compares it with the target host's own SMBIOS system UUID in the master's membership record. A mismatch, a host with no unique hardware identity and an unreadable controller each refuse the fence and power nothing off. Redirects are never followed, so the identity cannot be read from one machine while another is powered off. Core refuses a BMC profile whose host reports no unique hardware identity or which names no username, and refuses SCSI-PR outright. A refused profile's delivered password is released from the master's credential store.

credential.description: Optional material for the profile, never stored by the Controller. It is delivered over the existing one-time encrypted credential handoff, Core allocates its own private reference, and only that opaque reference is written into the command. Nothing reaches SQLite, the audit trail, the response or any log. A virsh profile takes {ssh_private_key, ssh_known_hosts}; redfish and ipmilan take {secret}, the password of the account named in the profile; a scsi_pr profile takes none. Omitting it means the profile must already name a credential_ref Core knows.

PoolFenceProfileRequest.description: Record or clear how a member of this pool would be power-fenced. Unknown fields are refused.

methods.description: At most one entry per kind.

recommended.description: The profile Core recommends recording; absent when no method can be recommended.

PoolBMCProbeResult.description: Which way one management controller answered the pool master, computed for one round trip and stored by no one. Recording a profile is still Set BMC access, which pins and proves the controller again.

target_ids.description: Redfish ComputerSystem Ids or IPMI plugs the controller reported, at most 16; empty when unreachable.

detail.description: Core's short sentence about this method, at most 512 bytes.

target_id.description: The system Id or plug to record.

request_id.description: Stable key for this Detect; it binds the one-time credential handoff. Use a new one for each Detect: the master retires a probe password after one use.

endpoint.description: The management controller address, a bare host name or IP address.

username.description: Optional account; given exactly when credential is.

credential.description: Optional {secret}: the account's password. Delivered to the pool master over the one-time encrypted credential handoff with probe-only bmc_probe purpose, never stored, logged, audited or echoed by the Controller. Core removes both temporary private copies after the probe or expires an undelivered handoff after 10 minutes on its local tick or next startup.

PoolBMCProbeRequest.description: Ask the pool master how a member's management controller answers. Unknown fields are refused.

error.description: Core's own sentence when status is failed; a failure with no text becomes "the pool master could not probe the management controller".

bmc_probe.description: The master's answer, mirrored verbatim. Always present when status is succeeded; may be present when it failed, to say what did answer.

PoolBMCProbeView.description: One brokered report round trip to the pool master. Nothing is stored, journalled or audited and no command is issued.

warnings.description: The same advisory sentences POST /api/v1/vms may answer with, present only on an operation whose kind is vm-create and whose status is dispatched. They are recomputed from the current mirror on every read and stored nowhere, so they disappear by themselves once the host's access is reported as current again. Every other field is unchanged.

OperationView.description: A durable operation as the listing reports it: the operation itself, plus advisory placement warnings recomputed on read for a VM create that is still dispatched. For backup-* operations host_id is the executing host (the restore target or the VM's owner) when the stored command names one, otherwise the pool master that queued it; the 202 and replay bodies of a queued request report the queueing host.

host_id.description: Host this report describes; set by the Controller relay.

observed_at.description: When the host read itself. Nothing is cached: every field is observed on request.

system_disk.description: The host's record of its system disk: where the running system started from and the latest replacement. Absent from a host that keeps none.

HostHardware.description: What a host reads about itself on request. State owner: Nex Core. Nothing here is cached, persisted or reported in a heartbeat, so a fresh Controller sees the same report as the one it replaced.

unavailable.description: The source for this section is missing or failed; the rest of the report is still returned.

reason.description: Which source could not be read, e.g. "dmidecode failed". The tool's own error text is never relayed: it can name paths.

serial.description: Returned to authenticated administrators only; never logged or written to a diagnostic bundle.

board_serial.description: Returned to authenticated administrators only; never logged.

HardwareSystem.description: The machine, its board, chassis and firmware, read from /sys/class/dmi/id.

unavailable.description: The source for this section is missing or failed; the rest of the report is still returned.

reason.description: Which source could not be read, e.g. "dmidecode failed". The tool's own error text is never relayed: it can name paths.

HardwareCPU.description: Processor model and topology from /proc/cpuinfo and the CPU topology sysfs.

unavailable.description: The source for this section is missing or failed; the rest of the report is still returned.

reason.description: Which source could not be read, e.g. "dmidecode failed". The tool's own error text is never relayed: it can name paths.

total_bytes.description: Installed total from the kernel. Still reported when the module table is unavailable: only the modules come from dmidecode.

HardwareMemory.description: Installed memory and, where dmidecode can be run, the module in each slot. At most 64 modules; a longer reply is refused as malformed.

MemoryModule.description: One DIMM slot; an empty slot reports its locator and a zero size.

unavailable.description: The source for this section is missing or failed; the rest of the report is still returned.

reason.description: Which source could not be read, e.g. "dmidecode failed". The tool's own error text is never relayed: it can name paths.

HardwareDisks.description: Whole block devices from lsblk. At most 128 devices; a longer reply is refused as malformed.

serial.description: Returned to authenticated administrators only; never logged.

HardwareDisk.description: One whole disk. Partitions and device-mapper devices are not reported here.

unavailable.description: The source for this section is missing or failed; the rest of the report is still returned.

reason.description: Which source could not be read, e.g. "dmidecode failed". The tool's own error text is never relayed: it can name paths.

HardwarePCI.description: PCI devices from lspci. At most 256 devices; a longer reply is refused as malformed.

address.description: Domain:bus:device.function, e.g. 0000:01:00.0. Temperature sensor labels name the same address.

class_id.description: Numeric class, for grouping GPUs, NICs and storage controllers without matching translated text.

PCIDevice.description: One PCI device, with the numeric ids beside their names.

unavailable.description: The source for this section is missing or failed; the rest of the report is still returned.

reason.description: Which source could not be read, e.g. "dmidecode failed". The tool's own error text is never relayed: it can name paths.

HardwareSensors.description: The temperature inputs the host's usage-history sampler records, at most 24. A host with no sensors reports an empty list, which is a normal state and not an error.

key.description: Identical to the StatsSeries key of this sensor's temperature series, so a gauge joins the two.

chip.description: hwmon chip name, e.g. coretemp, k10temp, drivetemp, nvme.

max_celsius.description: The chip's own tempN_max. Absent when the chip publishes no threshold; a gauge then shows a plain value with no warning band.

crit_celsius.description: The chip's own tempN_crit, used as the end of a gauge's scale. Absent when the chip publishes none.

TemperatureSensor.description: One temperature input with the chip's own thresholds, so a gauge takes its scale and warning band from the hardware rather than a number invented in the UI.

host_id.description: The other host of the pair. A member reports it as the host it checked; the pool master reports it back as the host that did the checking, because the checks are listed on the row of the host they are about.

result.description: ok: the controller answered, accepted the recorded account and named this host's own machine. unreachable: it did not answer, or did not report the machine it manages. credentials_rejected: it refused the recorded account. identity_mismatch: it named a different machine, which is not a network fault and never a pass. certificate_changed: it presented a certificate other than the one the profile is pinned to. tool_missing: this Nex Core has no ipmitool. no_profile: no fence device is recorded for that host. unusable: the profile could never produce a proof, for example a host with no unique hardware identity.

detail.description: Core's own sentence for that result, shown verbatim. Never a credential.

power.description: The machine's power state as the controller reported it; absent when the controller did not say. Reported, never acted on.

profile.description: Binds this result to the fence device it was taken against: 16 hex characters over the profile's kind, address, target, account, pinned certificate and cipher, plus the hardware identity it is compared with. The pool master drops every result whose stamp is not the one its membership records now, so a replaced profile cannot inherit the checks taken against the one before it and reads as not checked yet until the next pass.

observed_at.description: When the pool master last had this result confirmed, on the master's own clock, so freshness never depends on two hosts agreeing about the time. Set by the master; a member does not send it.

stale.description: The master has not had this result confirmed for longer than it vouches for (three check intervals). A stale check is shown as stale and is never readiness.

PoolFenceCheck.description: One host's non-destructive read of another host's fence device: the management controller's own report of which machine it manages, and whether that machine is powered on, over the recorded profile and the replicated credential. Nothing on that path can power anything off. It is a Core observation and never enters the master's durable membership record.

checks.description: At most 64 results, one per host the caller looked at. An entry naming the caller itself is dropped: a host does not get to say whether it can be shut out.

PoolFenceCheckRequest.description: One checking pass, as a member sends it to its pool master.

ready.description: How many of this pool's ready hosts another host could shut out.

total.description: How many ready hosts this pool has. An ejected host is a tombstone in the membership, not one of this pool's hosts, and a host that has not finished joining is not one either; neither is counted.

unready.description: The ready hosts no other host could shut out, by host ID.

host_fencing.description: The pool's Host fencing setting as the master records it. It is on for a pool that has never been told otherwise. On by itself arms nothing: Nex Core arms a host's watchdog only where every prerequisite below holds.

prerequisites.description: Core's own checklist for arming watchdogs, computed on the master over the membership it owns. A client displays it and decides no line of it.

cluster.description: The master's current cluster or qdevice status. This is a memory-only observation. A two-host qdevice may report forming or degraded while SBD arming and witness-loss proof remain withheld. Absent on older masters, which a client shows as no cluster line rather than as a cluster that is off.

PoolFenceSummary.description: The pool's own fencing answer, reported by the master with its membership: how many of this pool's hosts another host could shut out, which ones it could not, the Host fencing setting and Core's prerequisite checklist. A client displays it; it does not add up the rows it is about to render, which would count ejected tombstones and hosts that are still joining.

kind.description: The recorded fence profile's kind (ipmilan, redfish or virsh), or watchdog for the host's own self-fencing method. A host's row carries one entry per method.

state.description: ready: another ready host has a fresh successful check against this device. not_ready: Nex Core knows it would not work, and says why. unknown: Nex Core could not observe it, typically because nothing has checked this host yet. no_peer: this pool has no other host to be checked from, which is not a wait — a pool of one host also has nothing to promote over and needs no fence device. not_applicable: this pool cannot use this method at all, as a watchdog cannot be used below three hosts, and that is not something an operator can fix. Readiness is an observation shown to an operator: nothing here decides a promotion, which is decided by the live fence proof alone.

reason.description: Core's own sentence for a method that is not ready, shown verbatim. It names the host that found the problem, for example "this management controller did not answer (from host-b)".

checks.description: Every other ready host's last non-destructive read of this method against this host.

PoolFenceMethod.description: One way a host could be shut out, and whether it would work.

ready.description: At least one method is ready. No readiness at all, and readiness with no ready method, are both never treated as protected.

PoolFenceReadiness.description: The pool master's own per-method answer to whether this host could be shut out right now. It is derived from the membership the master owns and from the continuous non-destructive checks other hosts report, and is a memory-only observation overlaid on the membership copy the master reports, never part of the durable record. A master that has just restarted reports its methods as unknown until the next check pass rather than keeping a durable store of something one interval re-establishes.

state.description: What this host's own Nex Core found on its own management controller. provisioned: Core created its fence account and the master recorded the profile. no_local_interface: no /dev/ipmi0, so there is nothing to configure from the inside. user_management_refused: the controller refused in-band account management, or has no free user slot. lan_disabled: the controller reports no LAN address on any channel, or offers no authenticated RMCP+ cipher suite. name_conflict: an account under the Nex name exists that Core did not create, and nothing was changed. manual_profile: an operator entered a profile, which always wins. removed: an operator removed the account and automatic provisioning stays off for this host. pending_master: the account exists but the master has not recorded the profile yet, so this host has no usable fence device and is never shown as having one.

detail.description: Core's own sentence for that state, shown verbatim. Never a credential.

address.description: The controller's own LAN address as it reports it in-band.

channel.description: The controller's LAN channel the account was created on.

account.description: The account name Core created; not a secret. Its password goes to the master's private fence-credential store and nowhere else.

observed_at.description: When this finding last *changed*, not when it was last confirmed. An unchanged finding is deliberately not re-reported: the membership is signed and replicated, so a moving timestamp would re-sign and re-push the pool's whole authority every reconcile pass. It therefore says nothing about whether the host is still reporting. Liveness is that host's own connection, and the freshness of a fence device is PoolFenceCheck.observed_at, which the pool master stamps on its own clock every time a check is confirmed.

PoolHostBMC.description: One host's own report about its own management controller, kept in the pool master's membership record. It is a Core observation: a fresh Controller recovers it with the rest of the membership and stores nothing of its own. A member too old to report one is absent.

request_id.description: Stable client request ID. An exact retry answers with the same operation and never makes a second one.

PoolBMCProvisioningRequest.description: Let this host configure its own management controller for fencing again. There is no “off” here: clearing the fence device is what turns it off, through the one route that clears a profile.

name.description: Which line of the checklist this is: enough hosts for a majority side, a hardware watchdog on every host, a confirmed fence device on every host, and the pool's quorum.

state.description: unknown is Nex Core saying it cannot observe this yet and is never read as met. Quorum is unknown until this pool runs a quorum service.

detail.description: Core's own sentence for this line, shown verbatim, naming the hosts a line is unmet for.

hosts.description: Which hosts the sentence is about, as host IDs. Nex Core ends detail before naming them and puts them here, because only a client knows their display names.

PoolFencePrerequisite.description: One line of the prerequisite checklist Nex Core reports for arming watchdogs.

kind.description: Only a device that resets the machine independently of the kernel can count: hardware, and emulated where the host is itself a virtual machine and the hypervisor really does reset it. The kernel's softdog is software — a hung kernel does not run it — so it is reported and reported as not counting. A driver Nex Core does not recognise is unknown and counts as nothing until it is classified.

device.description: The sysfs device name, for example watchdog0. Not a path under /dev: Nex Core never opens the device node, because on most drivers opening it arms the timer.

driver.description: The kernel driver behind the device, which is what the classification is made on.

timeout_seconds.description: The device's configured timeout. Zero means the kernel did not say.
